title: [Proxy] CONNECT uses a second HTTP/1.1 head parser and the CONNECT/407 loop is implemented twice (HTTP and WebSocket transports)
body:
## Summary
ConnectReplyReader re-implements status-line and field parsing instead of using Http11ResponseParser, with different rules for version, field names, charset and Content-Length. The CONNECT request and 407 handling exists in both RawSocketTransport and ProxyTunnelConnector, with different wire headers, reconnect policy and drain caps. Fixes to one copy do not reach the others, which affects every HTTPS-through-proxy and WebSocket-through-proxy connection.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/ConnectReplyReader.cs:102`

## Problem
ConnectReplyReader.ReadCoreAsync (:102-134) re-implements status-line and field parsing instead of using Http11ResponseParser: it accepts any 'HTTP/' version (:243; the main parser admits only HTTP/1.x, Http11ResponseParser.cs:673-680), skips lines without a colon and trims names instead of rejecting obs-fold and non-token names (:126-130 versus :698-719), decodes ASCII (:358) instead of Latin-1, has its own Content-Length parser without duplicate detection (:267-283 versus :566-596), its own transfer-coding check (:285-293 versus :535-564) and treats a 1xx as the final reply. The stated reason is that it must not read past the header block (:66-68), which a reader able to hand back unread bytes would also satisfy. On top of the shared reader the handshake is duplicated: RawSocketTransport.EstablishConnectTunnelAsync / BuildConnectRequest / BuildProxyAuthorizationHeaderValue (RawSocketTransport.cs:1429-1568) and Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:48-190 (WriteConnectRequestAsync :141, BuildBasicAuthorization :184). The copies differ on the wire (HTTP sends 'Connection: keep-alive' at :1536, WebSocket sends 'Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive' at :150) and in policy (HTTP reconnects when the 407 is not reusable, :1482-1483; WebSocket fails, :120). Two unrelated drain caps exist for the same Basic-407 case: MaxProxyChallengeDrainBytes 64 KB (RawSocketTransport.cs:1688) and ConnectReplyReader.MaxDrainBytes 1 MB (:79). InternalsVisibleTo('TurboHTTP.WebSocket.Transport') (Runtime/Transport/AssemblyInfo.cs:5) is what lets the second copy exist.

**Failure scenario.** A parser hardening change (such as the obs-fold and Transfer-Encoding fixes of #41 and #40) lands in Http11ResponseParser only and the proxy-facing parser keeps the old behaviour. Concretely today a proxy reply 'HTTP/2 200' or a field line 'X Y: z' is accepted on CONNECT and rejected everywhere else, and the HTTP and WebSocket tunnels send different CONNECT requests to the same proxy, so a proxy quirk has to be diagnosed and fixed twice.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 9.3.6

## Suggested fix
Move the CONNECT exchange (request bytes, reply read, 407 policy, drain) into one Http1/ConnectTunnel type used by both transports, and parse the reply with the Http11ResponseParser status/field routines over a reader that can return unread bytes to the caller.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectReplyReader parses the reply head with the same rules as Http11ResponseParser (shared code or an equivalent reader that returns unread bytes)
- [ ] The CONNECT request builder, Proxy-Authorization value and 407 retry loop exist once and are used by both RawSocketTransport and ProxyTunnelConnector, with one drain cap
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering both callers

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The second parser exists as described: ConnectReplyReader.ReadCoreAsync (ConnectReplyReader.cs:102-134) accepts any 'HTTP/' prefix (:243) where the main parser admits only HTTP/1.x (Http11ResponseParser.cs:673-680), skips colon-less lines and trims names (:126-130) instead of rejecting them (:698-719), decodes ASCII (:358) not Latin-1, has its own Content-Length parser without duplicate detection (:267-283) and its own TE check (:285-293). A 1xx reply is treated as final and fails the tunnel (RawSocketTransport.cs:1513-1515), contrary to RFC 9110 Section 15.2, though proxies rarely send 1xx to CONNECT. The CONNECT loop is written twice: RawSocketTransport.cs:1429-1568 and WebSocket.Transport/ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:48-190; wire difference confirmed ('Connection: keep-alive' at RawSocketTransport.cs:1536 vs 'Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive' at ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:150) and policy difference confirmed (return null to reconnect at :1482-1483 vs throw at ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:119-125). Corrections that lower severity: the reader itself is already shared by both transports (deliberate, #229/#166, class comment :64-69) and only the ~60-line loop is duplicated; the WebSocket fail-instead-of-reconnect is a documented choice (ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:117-118); and the two drain caps are not for the same exchange (MaxProxyChallengeDrainBytes, RawSocketTransport.cs:1688, is the forward-proxy 407 parsed by Http11ResponseParser; MaxDrainBytes, ConnectReplyReader.cs:79, is the CONNECT 407). The leniencies ('HTTP/2 200', 'X Y: z') only affect a proxy-facing head whose body is ignored on 2xx, so no concrete harm beyond maintenance risk. #187 (fold WebSocket.Transport into Transport) is adjacent but does not track this.

Related: #162, [[R11-http1-protocol-18]], [[R11-http1-protocol-19]], [[R11-http1-runtime-10]].

title: [Proxy] ConnectReplyReader does not skip 1xx interim responses to CONNECT, so a 102/103 before the 200 fails the tunnel
body:
## Summary
ConnectReplyReader reads one status line and header block and returns it, treating a 1xx as the final reply. RawSocketTransport then fails with 'CONNECT tunnel failed with status N'. Users behind a proxy that sends an interim response before the final CONNECT reply cannot make HTTPS or WebSocket requests.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/ConnectReplyReader.cs:109`

## Problem
ReadCoreAsync reads exactly one status line and header block and returns it (ConnectReplyReader.cs:109-133); ParseStatusCode accepts 100-999 (240-265). EstablishConnectTunnelAsync treats anything that is not 2xx or 407 as failure: 'CONNECT tunnel failed with status N' (RawSocketTransport.cs:1512-1514). The main parser loops over interim responses (Http11ResponseParser.cs:243-254), this reader does not.

**Failure scenario.** A proxy that sends an interim response before the final CONNECT reply (for example 102/103 from an authenticating or policy proxy while it dials upstream) makes every HTTPS-through-proxy request, and the WebSocket proxy tunnel that shares the reader, fail with NetworkError although the 200 follows.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 15.2

## Suggested fix
Loop in ReadCoreAsync while the status is 1xx (bounded by Http11ResponseParser.Max1xxResponses and the existing header budget) before returning the final reply; add a ConnectReplyReaderTests case.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ConnectReplyReader skips 1xx replies (bounded by Http11ResponseParser.Max1xxResponses and the header budget) and returns the final reply
- [ ] A CONNECT answered with 103 then 200 establishes the tunnel; exceeding the bound fails with UHttpException NetworkError
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (ConnectReplyReaderTests case)

title: [Proxy] ConnectReplyReader accepts malformed field lines, can throw a raw ArgumentException, and judges 407 reuse from the first Connection/Content-Length line
body:
## Summary
The CONNECT reply reader skips lines without a colon, trims field names and accepts any 'HTTP/' prefix, unlike the main parser. A line such as ' :x' makes HttpHeaders.Add throw ArgumentException, which escapes as an Unknown error instead of a NetworkError. Connection and Content-Length are read from the first field line only, so a 407 can be judged reusable when a later line says close or lengths conflict.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/ConnectReplyReader.cs:126`

## Problem
Lines without a colon are skipped and names are Trim()med (ConnectReplyReader.cs:126-130), so 'Content-Length : 5' and a whitespace-led continuation ' Content-Length: 5' are accepted as fields, unlike the main parser (Http11ResponseParser.cs:698-723). A line ' :x' gives an empty name and HttpHeaders.Add throws ArgumentException (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:53-54), which escapes the documented 'UHttpException NetworkError' contract (85-88) and is mapped to UHttpErrorType.Unknown. The status line only needs the prefix 'HTTP/' (243). HasConnectionClose, HasContentLength and CanRetryOnSameConnection use Headers.Get, i.e. the first field line (41-61); several Content-Length values are not compared (180-185).

**Failure scenario.** A 407 with 'Connection: keep-alive' followed by a second line 'Connection: close', or with two different Content-Length values, is judged reusable: the client drains by the first length and re-sends CONNECT with Proxy-Authorization on a connection the proxy is closing or that is now misframed, and the request fails instead of reconnecting. A reply containing ' :x' surfaces as an Unknown error.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 4, 5.1, 6.3

## Suggested fix
Reuse the main parser's field-line rules (token names, no whitespace before the colon, reject obs-fold), wrap HttpHeaders failures in the reader's Fail(), require HTTP/1.x in the status line, and evaluate Connection/Content-Length over GetValues with the same duplicate check as TryGetValidatedContentLength.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Reply parsing rejects whitespace before the colon, obs-fold, non-token names and non-HTTP/1.x status lines with UHttpException NetworkError
- [ ] HttpHeaders failures are wrapped by the reader and never surface as UHttpErrorType.Unknown
- [ ] Connection and Content-Length reuse decisions evaluate all values; conflicting Content-Length or any 'close' makes the connection non-reusable
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (ConnectReplyReaderTests)

title: [Proxy] ConnectReplyReader issues one socket read per byte of the CONNECT reply
body:
## Summary
LineReader.ReadLineAsync awaits a one-byte ReadAsync for every byte of the CONNECT reply so as never to consume bytes past the header block. Each read is a syscall and a Task allocation, and on Mono may cost a thread-pool round trip. A 300-byte reply costs 300 reads per tunnel.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/ConnectReplyReader.cs:347`

## Problem
LineReader.ReadLineAsync awaits _stream.ReadAsync(_single, 0, 1, ct) for every byte (345-373); the class comment (65-68) explains the choice (never consume a byte past the header block). Each call is a Task<int>-returning socket read on the unbuffered proxy stream: a recv syscall per byte, and on Mono a thread-pool round trip whenever it does not complete synchronously. The header block cap is 16 KB (76).

**Failure scenario.** A proxy answers CONNECT with a 300-byte header block (Via, Proxy-Agent, Date...): 300 recv syscalls and Task<int> allocations per tunnel instead of one; on a mobile device this adds milliseconds to every new HTTPS-through-proxy connection, and a proxy can stretch it to 16384 reads.

## Suggested fix
Read in blocks and stop at the blank line, handing the unread tail to the TLS handshake through a small prefix stream (or, for a 2xx reply, peek the exact header length with MSG_PEEK-style reads on the socket).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The CONNECT reply head is read in blocks and any bytes after the blank line are handed to the TLS handshake without loss
- [ ] A 300-byte reply is read with at most 2 stream reads in a test using a counting stream
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering reply data that arrives together with tunnel payload bytes

title: [HTTP/1.1] Request validation runs inside serialization after a connection is leased, so an invalid request opens or destroys a healthy pooled connection
body:
## Summary
Header, trailer and body compatibility validation happens in Http11RequestSerializer, after RawSocketTransport has leased a connection. The exception disposes the lease, which destroys the connection even though nothing was written. An app that sends an invalid header on every request pays DNS, connect and TLS each time and also kills idle keep-alive connections. HTTP/2 validates before taking a stream.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:78`

## Problem
ValidateTrailerCompatibility (:78, 239-252) and HttpFieldValidator.ValidateField (:313, 331, 500) run from SerializeAsync / SerializeHeadersAsync, which RawSocketTransport calls only after _pool.GetConnectionAsync returned a lease (RawSocketTransport.cs:604, 1925, 2032). The exception leaves before any byte is written (the header writer is flushed at :102, after validation), but the finally blocks dispose the lease (RawSocketTransport.cs:742, 1195) and ConnectionLease.Dispose destroys the connection rather than pooling it (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:190, 223). HTTP/2 validates before a stream slot or id is taken (HttpFieldValidator.cs:34-37; Http2Connection.Send.cs:457). RawSocketTransportInvalidFieldTests.InvalidRequestHeader_FailsWithInvalidRequest_AndSendsNoBytes asserts that no bytes are sent, not that no connection is opened or lost.

**Failure scenario.** An app sets an Authorization header whose value ends with a newline (a token read from a file) on every request. Each call resolves DNS, connects and completes a TLS handshake, then fails with InvalidRequest and closes the socket; when an idle keep-alive connection exists, it is taken from the pool and destroyed although nothing was written to it.

## Suggested fix
Validate fields and trailer/body compatibility in DispatchCoreAsync before the dispatch loop, next to the URI and host checks (:443-471), sharing the HTTP/2 pre-check; keep the serializer checks as a backstop.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Field, trailer and body validation run in DispatchCoreAsync before a connection is leased, sharing the HTTP/2 pre-check
- [ ] An invalid request fails with InvalidRequest without opening a connection and without disposing a pooled one
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it asserting connection-open count and pool state

title: [HTTP/1.1] Unknown-length request bodies are always chunked, including on connections whose peer answered HTTP/1.0
body:
## Summary
ResolveBodyWriteMode sends Transfer-Encoding: chunked whenever the body length is unknown, and the pooled connection does not record the peer's HTTP version. A kept-alive connection to an HTTP/1.0 peer can therefore receive a chunked request, which that peer cannot parse and may interpret as further requests. Affects stream uploads to old servers and proxies.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:226`

## Problem
ResolveBodyWriteMode returns Chunked whenever content.Length has no value (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:225-227) and AppendHeaders writes 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' (346-349). Neither the serializer nor PooledConnection records the HTTP version a peer answered with (ParseStatusLine maps it to a local string only, Http11ResponseParser.cs:672-680), so a connection that previously answered HTTP/1.0 with keep-alive is reused for chunked uploads.

**Failure scenario.** Stream upload of unknown length to an HTTP/1.0-only server or proxy on a kept-alive connection: the peer sees a request without Content-Length, treats it as bodiless, and parses the chunk stream (whose payload may be user-generated content) as the next request on the connection. What would confirm it: an HTTP/1.0 keep-alive peer; with HTTP/1.1 peers the behaviour is correct.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 6.1

## Suggested fix
Remember on the pooled connection that the peer answered HTTP/1.0 and, for such a connection, either buffer the body to send Content-Length or send the chunked request on a fresh connection with Connection: close semantics; at minimum never reuse an HTTP/1.0 connection for a chunked request.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connection whose peer answered HTTP/1.0 is never used for a chunked request (fresh connection or buffered Content-Length body)
- [ ] HTTP/1.1 peers keep the current chunked behaviour
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it with an HTTP/1.0 keep-alive fake peer

title: [HTTP/1.1] A caller-supplied Host header is emitted verbatim, possibly several times and inconsistent with the absolute-form request target
body:
## Summary
When the caller sets Host, the serializer skips the generated line and writes every value, so two values yield two Host lines and the field is not first. With proxy absolute-form the target comes from the URI while Host keeps the caller value. Servers must answer 400 for multiple Host lines, and proxies and path filters can see different hosts.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:310`

## Problem
AppendHeaders skips the generated Host when request.Headers.Contains('Host') (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:310-317) and then writes every value of every caller header (320-337), so two Add('Host', ...) calls produce two Host lines and the field is no longer first. With RequestMetadataKeys.ProxyAbsoluteForm the request target is built from the URI (520-531) while Host keeps the caller value. The override is intentional (Http11SerializerTests.cs:134), but nothing bounds it to one value or keeps it consistent with the absolute-form target.

**Failure scenario.** A request with two Host values is rejected with 400 by any conforming server; through a forward proxy 'GET http://a.example/ HTTP/1.1' with 'Host: b.example' is routed by the proxy to a.example while Host-based access rules on the path see b.example.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 3.2, 3.2.2

## Suggested fix
Keep the override but emit exactly one Host line, first, reject more than one value as InvalidRequest, and for absolute-form requests send the URI authority (RFC 9112 Section 3.2.2) regardless of the override.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Exactly one Host line is emitted, first in the header block; more than one caller value fails with InvalidRequest
- [ ] For absolute-form requests the Host value equals the URI authority (RFC 9112 Section 3.2.2)
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (Http11SerializerTests cases)

title: [HTTP/1.1] Expect: 100-continue is still sent on a request with no content
body:
## Summary
For an empty body the serializer takes the one-shot path and copies the caller's Expect header, so 'Expect: 100-continue' goes out with no body. Strict servers answer 417 or 400, and the 417 is not retried without Expect because the retry requires an awaited expectation. Callers using WithExpectContinue with an empty body see the failure.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:320`

## Problem
ExpectContinueHelper.ShouldAwaitExpectContinue is false when the body is empty (ExpectContinueHelper.cs:8-27), so SendOnLeaseAsync uses the one-shot SerializeAsync (RawSocketTransport.cs:1912-1931), whose AppendHeaders copies every caller header except Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding/Trailer (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:320-337). The Expect field therefore goes out with no body and, per http1-protocol-02, no Content-Length. RawSocketTransportConnectionReuseTests.cs:92 exercises exactly this shape (POST, empty body, WithExpectContinue).

**Failure scenario.** client.Post(url).WithBody(empty).WithExpectContinue() sends 'Expect: 100-continue' with no content. Strict servers answer 417 or 400; the 417 is then not repeated without Expect because ShouldRetryWithoutExpectation requires ShouldAwaitExpectContinue (RawSocketTransport.cs:1666), so the caller sees the 417.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 10.1.1

## Suggested fix
Drop the 100-continue member of Expect in AppendHeaders when the resolved body write mode is None.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Expect: 100-continue is omitted when the resolved body write mode is None
- [ ] POST with an empty body and WithExpectContinue sends no Expect header and is not answered 417 by a strict fake server
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (Http11SerializerTests)

title: [HTTP/1.1] Request serialization boxes an enumerator per header and allocates two writer objects per request
body:
## Summary
AppendHeaders iterates Headers.Names and GetValues with foreach over interface types, boxing a struct enumerator per header name plus one, and allocates a PooledHeaderWriter and a PooledArrayBufferWriter per request. A request with 10 headers allocates about 450 bytes of enumerators plus wrapper objects, on a path the allocation gates target.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:329`

## Problem
AppendHeaders iterates 'foreach (var name in request.Headers.Names)' (320), an IEnumerable<string> over Dictionary.KeyCollection (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:108), and 'foreach (var value in values)' (329) over the IReadOnlyList<string> returned by GetValues (HttpHeaders.cs:81-86): each foreach boxes a struct enumerator (one per request plus one per header name). AppendRequestTrailers in the same file already uses an index loop (498). Each request also allocates a PooledHeaderWriter and a PooledArrayBufferWriter object (83, 539-544), and a chunked body a second pair for the trailer block (437).

**Failure scenario.** A request with 10 headers allocates 11 boxed enumerators (about 450 bytes) plus two wrapper objects on every send; small, but on the path the Phase 19 allocation gates target.

## Suggested fix
Use an index loop over GetValues, give HttpHeaders a struct enumerator or an internal allocation-free visitor for the serializer, and make PooledHeaderWriter a struct over a writer cached per connection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Header serialization allocates no enumerators (index loops or a struct enumerator/visitor) and writer wrappers are structs or cached per connection
- [ ] Allocations of serializing a 10-header request drop to 0 bytes beyond pooled buffers, measured by an allocation test
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it asserting the allocation bound (Tests/Runtime/Transport/)

title: [HTTP/1.1] POST/PUT/PATCH with an empty body are sent without Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding, and a caller-set Content-Length: 0 is stripped
body:
## Summary
For an empty body the serializer chooses write mode None and writes no framing, and IsFramingHeader removes any caller Content-Length. A POST, PUT or PATCH with no content goes out with no length. Servers and gateways that require a length (http.sys/IIS, S3-style PUT, several CDNs and WAFs) answer 411, and callers cannot work around it.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:340`

## Problem
ResolveBodyWriteMode returns RequestBodyWriteMode.None for an empty buffered body and for Length <= 0 (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:215-234). AppendHeaders writes Content-Length only for KnownLength (340-345) and removes every caller Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding through IsFramingHeader (322, 509-513), independent of the method. Tests only assert the GET case (Http11SerializerTests.cs:500) and that caller framing headers are stripped (625-637); RawSocketTransportConnectionReuseTests.cs:92 sends 'POST /empty' this way.

**Failure scenario.** client.Post(url).SendBufferedAsync() or a PUT with an empty body goes out as 'POST /x HTTP/1.1' with no Content-Length. Servers and gateways that require a length on methods that define content answer 411 Length Required (http.sys/IIS, S3-style PUT, several CDNs/WAFs), and the caller cannot work around it because headers.Set('Content-Length','0') is removed by the serializer.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 8.6

## Suggested fix
Emit 'Content-Length: 0' when the body is empty and the method is POST, PUT or PATCH (the methods HttpMethodExtensions.HasBody already names); keep omitting it for GET/HEAD/DELETE/OPTIONS. Add a serializer test per method.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Empty-body POST, PUT and PATCH requests send 'Content-Length: 0'; GET, HEAD, DELETE and OPTIONS do not
- [ ] A caller-set Content-Length: 0 on those methods is not stripped
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it with one serializer test per method (Http11SerializerTests)

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. EmptyRequestBody reports an empty buffered body (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequestBody.cs:257-269), ResolveBodyWriteMode returns None for it and for Length <= 0 (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:215-234), AppendHeaders emits Content-Length only for KnownLength (340-345) and drops any caller Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding via IsFramingHeader (322, 509-513) for every method. No method check exists anywhere in the serializer. Tests assert only the GET case (Http11SerializerTests.cs:502-510) and that a caller 'Content-Length: 0' is stripped (625-637). RFC 9110 Section 8.6: a user agent SHOULD send Content-Length when the method defines content, 'even when the value is 0' for POST. Raised to high: servers that answer 411 to a length-less POST/PUT (http.sys/IIS, S3 PUT) reject every empty-body POST/PUT/PATCH and the caller has no workaround because the header is removed.

title: [Core] Protocol defaults and character rules are duplicated across HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and Core (User-Agent version, token table, timeout message, trailer sets)
body:
## Summary
The 'TurboHTTP/1.0' User-Agent literal is hard-coded in three files and differs from the package version 1.0.0-pre.1. IsRfc9110TChar exists in both Transport and Core, the timeout message is built twice, header-rule lists live in two places, and TrailerFieldValidator holds two identical mutable internal HashSets. A fix in one copy leaves the others stale.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:356`

## Problem
'TurboHTTP/1.0' is hard-coded in Http11RequestSerializer.cs:356, Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Connection.cs:408 and Runtime/Unity/UnityExtensions.cs:143, while package.json:4 says 1.0.0-pre.1. IsRfc9110TChar exists in Runtime/Transport/Internal/EncodingHelper.cs:55-85 and again in Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:696-726 (the comment at :643-645 explains that Core cannot reference Transport, but Transport can use Core.Internal). The request-timeout message is built in RawSocketTransport.cs:832-836 and in Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:706-712. The transport-owned header rules live in two unrelated lists (IsFramingHeader, Http11RequestSerializer.cs:509-513; IsHttp2ForbiddenHeader, Http2Connection.Send.cs:560). TrailerFieldValidator keeps two identical 33-entry HashSets exposed as mutable internal statics (Runtime/Transport/Internal/TrailerFieldValidator.cs:8-50).

**Failure scenario.** The User-Agent product version has to be edited in three files at release and already differs from the package version; a token-rule fix in one IsRfc9110TChar copy leaves request-trailer name validation in Core different from header validation in Transport.

## Suggested fix

title: [Transport] HTTP/1.1 request writes are not raced against the cancellation token, so a stalled send may never end on IL2CPP
body:
## Summary
Serializer writes await stream.WriteAsync(ct) directly, and only Socket.Shutdown/Dispose ends a pending send when the token fires. Reads were moved to abandonable tasks because Mono and IL2CPP may never complete a pending operation after dispose. If sends behave the same, a stalled upload hangs past its timeout and holds the lease, permit and send buffer.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:395`

## Problem
Every serializer write awaits stream.WriteAsync(..., ct) directly (269, 395, 429-434, 629) and SendOnLeaseAsync awaits SerializeAsync (RawSocketTransport.cs:1925-1931). The only thing that ends a pending send when the request token fires is RegisterDisposeOnCancel's Socket.Shutdown + Dispose (312-325). For reads the code base stopped trusting exactly that: head reads go through AbandonableTask (#293), body reads through the reader race (#345), because 'Mono and IL2CPP may never end a pending socket read after ... the connection was disposed' and #384 measured reads that outlive shutdown on iOS. The stalled-upload test (RawSocketTransportTests.RequestTimeoutErrorModel.cs:45) runs in the Editor only.

**Failure scenario.** Large upload on a slow mobile link (send buffer full, WriteAsync pending in the IL2CPP I/O selector), then the request timeout or the caller's cancellation fires. If the runtime does not dispatch the pending send after the shutdown, as observed for receives, SerializeAsync never returns: DispatchAsync hangs past its timeout and the lease, the per-host permit and the pooled send buffer stay held. Needs a device run (iOS/Android IL2CPP, peer that stops reading, cancel mid-upload) to confirm or refute.

## Suggested fix
Run the stalled-upload timeout test on IL2CPP devices and record it in the #99 matrix; if a pending send can outlive the shutdown, race the write like the reads (abandon the task, keep the send buffer out of the pool until it ends).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The stalled-upload timeout test is run on iOS and Android IL2CPP devices and recorded in the #99 matrix
- [ ] If a send can outlive shutdown, writes are raced against the token like reads and the lease, permit and buffer are released on timeout

title: [HTTP/1.1] Chunked request bodies cost three stream writes per chunk and small streamed bodies are not coalesced with the header block
body:
## Summary
WriteChunkedBodyAsync writes the size line, the data and the CRLF separately for each chunk, plus a fourth write for the terminator. With TCP_NODELAY this produces three segments (or TLS records) per chunk, and a known-length streamed body is written after a separate header write. Uploads from producers yielding small reads multiply the cost.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:429`

## Problem
WriteChunkedBodyAsync writes the chunk-size line, the chunk data and the 2-byte CRLF with three separate stream.WriteAsync calls per chunk (429-434), then the last-chunk/trailer block with a fourth (437-441). The stream is the unbuffered socket stream (HoldingNetworkStream/SaeaStream/PollSelectStream, TcpConnectionPool.cs:660-672) with TCP_NODELAY on (Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:491), or a TLS stream on top of it. The coalescing that exists (TryWriteSmallBufferedRequestAsync, 184-199) only covers bodies that are already buffered; a known-length body read from a session is written after a separate header write (102, 395) however small it is.

**Failure scenario.** Upload of an unknown-length stream body: every chunk becomes three send syscalls and, with NoDelay, three TCP segments (a 3-10 byte one, the data, a 2 byte one); over TLS three records, i.e. two extra AEAD operations and about 58 bytes of record overhead per chunk. A producer that yields small reads (a pipe, a JSON-lines generator) multiplies this per read: a 100-byte read costs three packets.

## Suggested fix
Reserve room for the chunk-size line in front of the body buffer and for CRLF behind it (rent bodyBuffer with a 10+2 byte margin, read the session into the middle) and send each chunk with one write; fold the terminating CRLF of the last data chunk into the trailer writer. Append a first small session read to the header writer when it fits under SmallBufferedRequestThresholdBytes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each chunk is sent with one stream write (size line, data and CRLF in one buffer)
- [ ] The first small body read is coalesced with the header block when it fits, and the terminating CRLF is folded into the trailer write
- [ ] A 100-byte chunk produces 1 write call in a counting-stream test
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it asserting write counts

title: [HTTP/1.1] A request trailer on the prohibited list is silently dropped while its name is still announced in the Trailer header
body:
## Summary
The Trailer header lists every declared name, but AppendRequestTrailers skips names in the prohibited set (for example Content-Type, Date, Expires, Retry-After) with a bare continue, in both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. The server sees a declared trailer that never arrives and the developer gets no error or event.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:494`

## Problem
Core validates declared trailer names for token syntax only and defers the prohibited list to the transport (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:641-658). AppendDeclaredTrailerHeader writes every declared name (:462-479), then AppendRequestTrailers skips names in TrailerFieldValidator.ProhibitedRequestTrailers with a bare continue (:494-495; the same in Http2Connection.Send.cs:432-433). The set contains fields a caller may plausibly send as trailers, such as Content-Type, Date, Expires and Retry-After (Runtime/Transport/Internal/TrailerFieldValidator.cs:20-43). No event is recorded on the RequestContext and nothing is thrown, unlike an invalid field (HttpFieldValidationException mapped to InvalidRequest).

**Failure scenario.** request.WithRequestTrailers(['X-Checksum', 'Expires'], provider): the wire carries 'Trailer: X-Checksum, Expires' and only X-Checksum in the trailer section; the server and the developer both see a declared trailer that never arrives, with nothing in the logs or the request timeline.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 6.5.1

## Suggested fix
Reject prohibited names when they are declared (move the list to Core.Internal so WithRequestTrailers can throw ArgumentException), or at least omit them from the Trailer header and record a context event when a trailer is dropped.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Prohibited trailer names are rejected when declared (ArgumentException from WithRequestTrailers) or omitted from the Trailer header with a recorded context event
- [ ] The Trailer header never names a field that is not sent, on HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2

title: [HTTP/1.1] Http11RequestSerializer writes the request-target to the wire without validating it
body:
## Summary
Http11RequestSerializer validates header names, header values and the host, but appends the request-target from Uri.PathAndQuery between the method and HTTP/1.1 unchecked. Safety depends entirely on System.Uri escaping on every Unity runtime and construction mode. If a runtime returns a raw space, CR or LF, the request line is split and attacker-chosen lines reach the connection.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11RequestSerializer.cs:520`

## Problem
GetRequestTarget returns Uri.PathAndQuery (or scheme + authority + PathAndQuery for absolute-form) and AppendHeaders appends it between the method and ' HTTP/1.1' (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:303-306, 520-535). Header names and values go through HttpFieldValidator (331, 500) and the host through WireHost (312-313), but no check rejects SP, CR, LF, other CTLs or bytes above 0x7E in the target; PooledHeaderWriter.Append only rejects characters above U+00FF (EncodingHelper.cs:35-43). Safety rests entirely on System.Uri escaping on every runtime (Mono, IL2CPP) and construction mode (e.g. the obsolete dontEscape constructor, custom UriParser subclasses).

**Failure scenario.** If any supported runtime returns a PathAndQuery containing a raw space or CR LF for some input (a URL assembled from user-generated content is the usual source), the request line is split and attacker-chosen header lines or a second request are written to the connection. What would confirm it: a Uri whose PathAndQuery contains 0x20/0x0D/0x0A on Unity 2021.3 Mono or IL2CPP.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 3, 3.2

## Suggested fix
Validate the target once in AppendHeaders (reject anything outside 0x21-0x7E, report InvalidRequest via HttpFieldValidationException) and add a serializer test with a hostile PathAndQuery through a Uri test double.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The serializer rejects a request-target containing any byte outside 0x21-0x7E with an InvalidRequest error (HttpFieldValidationException) before writing anything
- [ ] Valid targets, including percent-encoded paths and queries and absolute-form targets, serialize unchanged

title: [HTTP/1.1] StreamingOptions.DefaultStreamingReceiveBufferBytes only sizes the drain buffer, not the socket receive buffers
body:
## Summary
The only reader of DefaultStreamingReceiveBufferBytes in Runtime is Http11ResponseBodySource, which uses it for the buffer rented while draining. The buffers that receive from the socket are hard-coded (BufferedStreamReader 4096 bytes head buffer, 64 KB body read cap), and HTTP/2 ignores the option. A developer tuning download throughput or memory sees no effect, and the public property has no XML documentation.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:64`

## Problem
The only reader of the option in Runtime/ is Http11ResponseBodySource (:64), which uses it for the buffer DrainAsync rents (:238) and as an upper bound in DrainWithinBudgetAsync (:478). The buffers that actually receive from the socket are BufferedStreamReader.DefaultBufferSize = 4096 and MaxBodyReadBufferBytes = 64 KB (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1040-1041, 1320-1321); HTTP/2 does not read the option. The public property has no XML documentation (Runtime/Core/StreamingOptions.cs:41).

**Failure scenario.** A developer tuning download throughput or memory sets DefaultStreamingReceiveBufferBytes to 256 KB (or to 4 KB on a low-memory device): streaming reads are unchanged, only the size of the throwaway drain buffer changes.

## Suggested fix
Either wire the option into BufferedStreamReader (head buffer and body buffer cap) or rename and document it as the drain buffer size.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Either the option sizes the BufferedStreamReader head and body buffers, or it is renamed and documented as the drain buffer size
- [ ] The property has XML documentation stating exactly what it controls and for which protocol
- [ ] A test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ asserts the chosen behavior (buffer size observed through the reader or drain path)

title: [HTTP/1.1] Draining a discarded response body copies every byte through two pooled 64 KB buffers
body:
## Summary
DrainAsync and DrainWithinBudgetAsync read into a rented 64 KB destination buffer. With a cancellable token the read first lands in the reader-owned body buffer (up to 64 KB) and is then copied into the drain buffer, only to be discarded. Every discarded redirect or early-disposed body therefore rents two 64 KB arrays and copies the data once more than needed.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:238`

## Problem
DrainAsync rents _drainBufferBytes (64 KB by default) and loops ReadAsync into it (238-246); DrainWithinBudgetAsync does the same for the dispose drain (478-492). With a cancellable token, which the dispose drain always has (295-298), a read of 4096 bytes or more first goes into the reader-owned _bodyBuffer, itself rented at up to 64 KB, and is then copied into the drain buffer (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1320-1328), only to be thrown away.

**Failure scenario.** Discarding the 40 KB body of a redirect or of an early-disposed response rents two 64 KB arrays and copies the 40 KB once more than needed, per discarded response.

## Suggested fix
Add a SkipAsync/discard read to BufferedStreamReader that reads into its own buffer and advances without copying, and let DrainAsync/DrainWithinBudgetAsync use it instead of renting a destination.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] BufferedStreamReader offers a skip/discard read that advances without copying, and both drain paths use it without renting a destination buffer
- [ ] Draining a 40 KB body performs zero extra copies and rents no drain buffer; measured with an allocation/copy assertion in a test
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering drain correctness (bytes consumed, connection reusable)

title: [HTTP/1.1] Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync during a pending read starts a second concurrent read on the same BufferedStreamReader
body:
## Summary
UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync awaits the body source's DisposeAsync without checking for a read in flight. For keep-alive chunked bodies, or Content-Length remainders up to 64 KB, the dispose drain issues a second read through the same reader while the consumer's read is suspended. The drain resets shared value-task state and buffer offsets, drops the first reader's continuation and can leave the first ReadAsync never completing.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:279`

## Problem
UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync -> DisposeAsyncCore awaits _bodySource.DisposeAsync() with no check for a read in flight (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:111-118, 227-232). Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync (279-316) only checks _terminalState; with keep-alive and a chunked body (ShouldAttemptDisposeDrain always true, 460-463) or <= 64 KB of Content-Length left it calls DrainWithinBudgetAsync -> ReadAsync (470-492). That re-enters ReadChunkedAsync/ReadContentLengthAsync and the reader while the consumer's read is suspended inside them: FillBufferAsync resets _start/_end to 0 (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1366-1367) and issues a second _stream.ReadAsync into the same _buffer; ReadBodyAsync then calls _bodyReadCore.Reset() and overwrites _bodyReadAwaiter/_bodyReadToken/_bodyReadRegistration (1419-1426). Reset() clears the continuation the first reader registered and bumps the version, and OnBodyReadCompleted (1431-1455) reads _bodyReadAwaiter, which now belongs to the second read, so the first read's completion calls GetResult() on a task that may not be complete (a blocking wait on the I/O completion thread). _chunkBytesRemaining/_awaitingChunkTerminator (non-volatile, 36-39) are mutated by both flows.

**Failure scenario.** One task loops 'await body.ReadAsync(buf, token)' on a keep-alive chunked stream and is waiting for the next chunk; another task calls 'await response.DisposeAsync()' to stop it. The drain issues a second read on the socket and resets the value-task source: the first reader's continuation is dropped, so its ReadAsync never completes (or throws InvalidOperationException for a stale token), chunk framing state is consumed by the wrong flow, and after the 2 s drain timeout the body is closed with the first read still unresolved. With TLS the second read can instead fail with the stream's 'read already in progress' error, which lands in DisposeAsync's catch-all and falls into the Abort path of http1-runtime-01.

## Suggested fix
Track 'read in flight' in the body source (one Interlocked flag set around ReadAsync) and make DisposeAsync skip the drain and take the abort path when it is set; never start a drain read while another read owns the reader. Cover it with a test that disposes asynchronously while a read is pending on a stream that never answers.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Http11ResponseBodySource tracks a read in flight (Interlocked) and DisposeAsync skips the drain and takes the abort path when a read is pending
- [ ] No second socket read is started while another read owns the reader; the pending read completes or fails with a defined error (cancellation/abort), never hangs
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it that disposes asynchronously while a read is pending on a stream that never answers

## Context

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync -> DisposeAsyncCore awaits _bodySource.DisposeAsync() with no in-flight check (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:111-118, 227-237). Http11ResponseBodySource.DisposeAsync checks only _terminalState (279-283); for keep-alive chunked bodies ShouldAttemptDisposeDrain is always true (460-463), so DrainWithinBudgetAsync -> ReadAsync (492) re-enters ReadChunkedAsync and the reader while the consumer's read is suspended. FillBufferAsync zeroes _start/_end (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1366-1367) and ReadBodyAsync issues a second _stream.ReadAsync into the same _buffer, then Reset()s _bodyReadCore and overwrites _bodyReadAwaiter/_bodyReadToken/_bodyReadRegistration (1415-1426): the first reader's registered continuation is dropped, and the first read's OnBodyReadCompleted (1431-1455) takes the second read's awaiter, calls GetResult on it, and the second completion then falls into the 'abandoned' branch and disposes the stream (1459-1470). Nothing in the body source tracks a read in flight. The class comment (lines 12-13) puts the duty on the caller, but the sync Dispose path tolerates a concurrent read (Abort) and the async one does not. Needs a consumer that calls DisposeAsync from another flow during a pending read, so medium.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Close-delimited response body over SslStream is reported complete on any EOF, so truncation can go undetected
body:
## Summary
Read-until-close bodies treat a zero-byte read as normal completion, and nothing under Runtime/Transport outside BouncyCastle checks whether the TLS closure was clean. The BouncyCastle path requires close_notify, the default SslStream path has no equivalent check. An on-path attacker that cuts the TCP connection could hand the caller a 200 with a silently shortened body, if SslStream returns 0 on EOF without close_notify on Unity Mono/IL2CPP.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:389`

## Problem
Http11ResponseBodySource.ReadToEndAsync treats read == 0 as normal completion (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:389-400); nothing in the HTTP/1.1 layer asks the connection whether the TLS closure was clean. The BouncyCastle provider does enforce it (TurboTlsClient.RequiresCloseNotify() => true, Runtime/Transport/BouncyCastle/TurboTlsClient.cs:99-102, EOF without close_notify throws an IOException), but the default SslStream path has no equivalent check anywhere under Runtime/Transport (rg close_notify finds only BouncyCastle files). RFC 9112 Section 9.8: 'A response that has neither chunked transfer coding nor Content-Length is complete only if a valid closure alert has been received.'

**Failure scenario.** HTTPS response without Content-Length or chunked coding (HTTP/1.0 origin, some streaming/CGI endpoints). An on-path attacker injects a TCP FIN/RST after N bytes. With an SslStream implementation that returns 0 on transport EOF, the caller receives a 200 with a silently shortened body (truncated JSON/config/asset) and no error. What would confirm it: SslStream.ReadAsync on Unity Mono/IL2CPP returning 0 (not throwing) when the peer closes TCP without close_notify.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.8

## Suggested fix
Expose 'closed cleanly' from the connection stream abstraction (true for cleartext FIN and for a received close_notify) and make the ReadToEnd body kind fail with a NetworkError when a TLS connection ended without it. Add a test with a TLS loopback server that drops the socket without close_notify mid-body.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The connection stream abstraction exposes whether the connection closed cleanly (cleartext FIN or received close_notify)
- [ ] A TLS read-to-close body that ends without a clean closure fails with a NetworkError (UHttpException) instead of completing
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it with a TLS loopback server that drops the socket without close_notify mid-body
- [ ] Behavior of SslStream on EOF without close_notify is validated on Unity Mono and IL2CPP and recorded

## Context

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Whether the default SslStream path returns 0 or throws on a TCP close without close_notify on Unity Mono/IL2CPP cannot be settled statically. title: [HTTP/1.1] DisposeAsync of an unfinished keep-alive chunked response always attempts a network drain and can stall for 2 s
body:
## Summary
ShouldAttemptDisposeDrain returns true for every keep-alive chunked body, so DisposeAsync reads from the socket under a 2 s timeout. For an SSE or long-poll response whose server is idle, the caller waits the full 2 s before the connection is closed anyway, and the per-host connection permit stays held for that time. Sync Dispose aborts immediately, so the two paths behave very differently.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:460`

## Problem
ShouldAttemptDisposeDrain returns true for every keep-alive chunked body (460-463); DisposeAsync then runs DrainWithinBudgetAsync under a 2 s CancelAfter (20, 292-300), reading from the socket until 64 KB of wire budget is used or the timeout fires. UHttpStreamingResponse.DisposeAsync always takes this path (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:227-232), while sync Dispose aborts at once (157-159). Http11DisposeDrainCancellationTests pins the 2 s bound as intended for a stalled peer.

**Failure scenario.** A consumer of a server-sent-events or long-poll chunked response leaves its read loop and exits an 'await using' block while the server is idle: DisposeAsync waits the full 2 s for bytes that do not come, then closes the connection anyway; the per-host connection permit stays held for those 2 s and the caller's continuation is delayed by them on every such teardown.

## Suggested fix
Drain only what is already available without waiting (reader-buffered bytes plus Socket.Available), or stop the drain as soon as a read would pend; keep the timed drain only for Content-Length bodies with a small known remainder.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] DisposeAsync drains only data already available (reader-buffered bytes, Socket.Available) and stops as soon as a read would pend
- [ ] The timed drain remains only for Content-Length bodies with a small known remainder
- [ ] DisposeAsync of an idle chunked stream completes without waiting for the 2 s drain timeout

title: [HTTP/1.1] Buffered responses create a redundant linked CancellationTokenSource per response when the caller passes a token
body:
## Summary
GetEffectiveReadToken links the caller's read token with the transport token whenever both are cancellable and differ. In buffered mode the transport token is already a link of that same caller token, so the second link adds a CancellationTokenSource, two registrations and a lock acquisition per read without covering any new cancellation source.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:653`

## Problem
GetEffectiveReadToken links the read token with _transportReadToken whenever both can be cancelled and differ (640-657). In buffered mode the collector reads with the caller's token (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/BufferedDispatchBridge.cs:25-30, ResponseCollectorHandler.cs:180) while the transport token is the request timeout CTS, which DispatchCoreAsync already created as a link of that same caller token (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-441, passed down at 1826-1840). The second link adds a CTS and two registrations per response and a lock acquisition per read (643), without covering any cancellation source the transport token does not already cover.

**Failure scenario.** Any SendBufferedAsync call with a cancellable token (for example a MonoBehaviour's destroy token) and a response body: one extra linked CTS with two registrations is created and disposed per response, and each body read takes _tokenLock.

## Suggested fix
Pass the caller's token to the body source alongside the transport token (DispatchOnLeaseAsync can receive it like the HTTP/2 path does) and read with the transport token alone when the read token is that caller token; keep ct.IsCancellationRequested for the timeout-vs-cancel classification.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The body source reads with the transport token alone when the read token is the caller token already linked into it

title: [HTTP/1.1] Bytes after a complete response in the reader buffer are discarded and the connection is pooled as clean
body:
## Summary
BufferedStreamReader reads up to 4 KB regardless of message framing. When a body completes, the reader is disposed and the lease returned to the pool without checking for unread buffered bytes; the same happens for HEAD/204/304/Content-Length: 0 and for a drained proxy 407. Extra bytes from a misbehaving or injected peer are dropped, and the rest are parsed as the response to the next request on that connection, enabling a forged or malformed response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:660`

## Problem
BufferedStreamReader.FillBufferAsync reads up to the whole 4 KB buffer regardless of message framing (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1364-1399), in the head phase and for small body reads (1331-1338). When the body completes, CompleteBody disposes the reader and calls _lease.ReturnToPool() (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:660-674); for HEAD/204/304/Content-Length: 0 this happens in the constructor (82-86). BufferedStreamReader.Dispose (1090-1111) returns the buffer without checking _end > _start, and the reader exposes no 'has buffered data' query. The same happens after a drained proxy 407 (RawSocketTransport.cs:1798 'using var head' then CompleteLeaseDispatch -> ReturnToPool, 1701-1703). The only later guard is TcpConnectionPool.HasUnexpectedData (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:802-808), which looks at Socket.Available, i.e. kernel bytes only; its own comment says it cannot see plaintext already buffered in the TLS stream.

**Failure scenario.** A peer (misbehaving origin that sends a body on a HEAD/304 response, an origin with a header-injection bug, or a desynchronised intermediary) sends response A followed by extra bytes X in the same read. A is delivered, the part of X that reached the reader buffer is thrown away, and the connection is reused. Whatever part of X was not in that buffer (still in transit, or sitting decrypted inside the TLS stream where Socket.Available is 0) is parsed as the status line/response of the next, unrelated request on that connection: either a forged response is attributed to it, or it fails with 'Malformed HTTP response' and is not retried (FormatException is not a stale-connection failure).

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.3 (persistence requires a self-defined message length on both sides)

## Suggested fix
Give BufferedStreamReader a HasBufferedData property and make Http11ResponseBodySource.CompleteBody (and the proxy-407 drain path) dispose the lease instead of pooling it when unread bytes remain after the message end. Add a test: 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 1, body a' immediately followed by a second response in the same write must not leave a pooled connection.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] BufferedStreamReader exposes whether unread buffered data remains, and CompleteBody and the proxy-407 drain path close the connection instead of pooling it when data remains after the message end
- [ ] A connection with trailing bytes after a response is never reused
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it where a second response follows the first in the same write and no pooled connection remains

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Head-phase and framing reads fill the whole 4 KB reader buffer regardless of message length (Http11ResponseParser.cs FillBufferAsync 1364-1399, ReadAsync 1331). CompleteBody disposes the reader and pools the lease (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:660-671; from the constructor for Empty/Content-Length 0 at 82-86). BufferedStreamReader.Dispose (1090-1111) returns the buffer without looking at _end > _start and the type has no buffered-data accessor (rg HasBuffered|Buffered finds none). Same for the drained 407 (RawSocketTransport.cs:1798, 1809-1823 -> CompleteLeaseDispatch 1701-1703). The only later guard, HasUnexpectedData, reads Socket.Available (TcpConnectionPool.cs:802-808) and its own comment says it cannot see plaintext buffered in the TLS stream. So leftover bytes split between the reader buffer and SslStream's decrypted record (or bytes still in flight) are attributed to the next request. Needs a misbehaving or injectable peer, so medium. No test with trailing bytes after a keep-alive response exists.

Also reported as `http1-runtime-03` (merged into this issue).

title: [HTTP/1.1] Response header limits are private constants and disagree with HTTP/2, CONNECT and WebSocket limits
body:
## Summary
Http11ResponseParser hard-codes an 8192-byte line limit, 102400 total header bytes, 32 KB trailers, 10 interim responses and a 256-byte chunk-size line, with no option to change them. HTTP/2 exposes Http2Options.MaxHeaderListSize (64 KB default), and CONNECT and WebSocket use other fixed limits. A single 10 KB field line works over HTTP/2 but fails every attempt over HTTP/1.1 as a retryable NetworkError, so the retry module repeats a deterministic failure.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:156`

## Problem
MaxHeaderLineLength = 8192, MaxTotalHeaderBytes = 102400, MaxTotalTrailerBytes = 32 KB and Max1xxResponses = 10 (Http11ResponseParser.cs:156-160) and the chunk-size line cap of 256 (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:16, Http11ResponseParser.cs:866) are compile-time constants; RawSocketTransport passes no limit to the parser and neither StreamingOptions nor ConnectionPoolOptions has an HTTP/1.1 header setting. HTTP/2 exposes Http2Options.MaxHeaderListSize (Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:106; default 64 KB, Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Settings.cs:18), CONNECT replies use 8 KB per line and 16 KB per block (ConnectReplyReader.cs:73-76) and the WebSocket handshake 8 KB in total (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:114). An over-limit head is a FormatException mapped to NetworkError 'Malformed HTTP response: HTTP header line exceeds maximum length' (RawSocketTransport.cs:809-813), which is retryable.

**Failure scenario.** An origin that sends one 10 KB field line (a large Content-Security-Policy, a Set-Cookie carrying a signed session, a long Link or Report-To) works over HTTP/2 (64 KB list limit, configurable) and fails on every attempt over HTTP/1.1 with a retryable NetworkError and no way to raise the limit; conversely 80 KB of small headers pass on HTTP/1.1 and are refused on HTTP/2 by default. The application sees protocol-dependent failures it cannot configure away.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 2.3; RFC 9110 Section 5.4

## Suggested fix
Add HTTP/1.1 limits to the transport options (max field-line bytes, max header bytes, max trailer bytes, max interim responses), default them consistently with Http2Options.MaxHeaderListSize, pass them to the parser and body source, and report an over-limit head as a non-retryable error.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HTTP/1.1 limits (field-line bytes, header bytes, trailer bytes, interim responses) are configurable in the transport options with defaults consistent with Http2Options.MaxHeaderListSize
- [ ] The limits are passed to the parser and body source, and an over-limit head fails with a non-retryable error
- [ ] The new options have XML documentation
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it for raising and lowering each limit

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Constants are compile-time and unreachable from options: MaxHeaderLineLength 8192, MaxTotalTrailerBytes 32 KB, MaxTotalHeaderBytes 102400, Max1xxResponses 10 (Http11ResponseParser.cs:156-160), chunk-size line 256 (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:16; Http11ResponseParser.cs:866). The head parser applies them directly (:272, :282, :293-295) and no Core option carries an HTTP/1.1 header limit (rg for MaxHeader in Runtime/Core finds only Http2Options.MaxHeaderListSize, Http2Options.cs:106; default 64 KB at Http2Settings.cs:18). CONNECT uses 8 KB/16 KB (ConnectReplyReader.cs:73-76), the WebSocket handshake 8 KB (WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:114). An over-limit line throws FormatException('HTTP header line exceeds maximum length') (:1163, :1177, :1529), mapped to NetworkError 'Malformed HTTP response: ...' (RawSocketTransport.cs:809-813), and UHttpError.IsRetryable returns true for NetworkError (UHttpError.cs:72-74), so the retry module repeats a deterministic failure. Scenario holds: a single field line over 8,192 bytes passes on HTTP/2 (64 KB list, configurable) and fails every time on HTTP/1.1 with no way to raise the limit; the reverse case (about 80 KB of small fields) passes on HTTP/1.1 and is rejected on HTTP/2 by default (ReadLoop.cs:610-620). 8 KB per line meets the RFC 9112 Section 2.3 recommendation of at least 8000 octets, so this is a configurability/consistency defect, not a protocol violation; lines that long are uncommon but occur (large CSP, Link, Report-To). No open issue tracks it (#121 covers other client options).

Related: #121, [[R11-http1-protocol-11]].

title: [HTTP/1.1] HeaderParseScratch pooling saves no allocation and is rented across the status-line network wait
body:
## Summary
ParseNextHeadDataAsync rents a HeaderParseScratch before awaiting the status line, collects pairs into it and then copies them into a new HttpHeaders, which allocates its own lists anyway. The scratch removes no allocation, adds two pool lock acquisitions per response, and is held by every in-flight request, so beyond 16 concurrent requests the pool misses and allocates.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:266`

## Problem
ParseNextHeadDataAsync rents a HeaderParseScratch (266) before awaiting the status line (272), collects (name, value) pairs in it (297) and then copies them one by one into a new HttpHeaders (300-302), which allocates its own List<string> per name anyway. The scratch therefore removes no allocation (its doc in Runtime/Core/Internal/HeaderParseScratchPool.cs:10-15 claims it 'reduces per-request list allocations'); it adds two acquisitions of the pool's global lock (ObjectPool.Rent/Return) and a second pass per response head. Because it is rented before the first read, each in-flight request holds one for its whole time-to-first-byte; the pool capacity is 16.

**Failure scenario.** More than 16 concurrent HTTP/1.1 requests waiting for their response heads: every further request misses the pool, allocates a scratch with a 16-entry list and has it discarded on return, so the pool is empty exactly under the concurrency it was sized for, while all requests still serialize on its lock twice per response.

## Suggested fix
Add the parsed pairs to the HttpHeaders directly and delete the scratch pool; if it is kept, rent it only after the status line has been read.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Parsed header pairs are added directly to HttpHeaders and the HeaderParseScratch pool is removed (or rented only after the status line is read)
- [ ] Per-response head parsing performs no scratch pool lock acquisitions; allocation count per head does not increase, measured in a test or benchmark
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it confirming parsed headers are unchanged

title: [HTTP/1.1] A blank first line from the server is handled as 'connection closed before the status line' by matching an exception message
body:
## Summary
ParseNextHeadDataAsync throws the same FormatException('Empty HTTP status line') for EOF before any byte and for an empty line, and RawSocketTransport recognizes the stale-connection case by comparing that message text. A stray CRLF from a server on a reused connection causes a live connection to be dropped and the request replayed, and a genuine close is reported as a malformed response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:273`

## Problem
ParseNextHeadDataAsync throws FormatException('Empty HTTP status line') for both null (EOF before any byte) and '' (the peer sent CRLF) (Http11ResponseParser.cs:272-274). RawSocketTransport.IsConnectionClosedBeforeStatusLine recognises the stale-connection case by comparing that message string (RawSocketTransport.cs:380-387) and feeds IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure (356-363) and ShouldSurfaceCommittedNonReplayableBodyFailure (365-378).

**Failure scenario.** On a reused connection a server that emits a stray CRLF before its status line (a known legacy quirk after POST bodies) makes the client drop a live connection and replay the request on a new one, recorded as TransportRetryStale; on a fresh connection a genuine close without any response is reported as 'Malformed HTTP response: Empty HTTP status line' rather than a connection-closed error.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 2.2, 9.3.1

## Suggested fix
Return a distinct, typed signal for EOF-before-first-byte (dedicated exception type or a result flag) and treat a received empty line as a malformed response (or skip one leading CRLF), instead of string-matching a shared message.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] EOF before the first byte is signalled by a distinct typed exception or result flag, and the transport no longer matches on message text
- [ ] A received empty line is treated as malformed, or one leading CRLF is skipped, per the chosen rule
- [ ] A genuine close without a response is reported as a connection-closed error rather than 'Malformed HTTP response'
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it for both cases

title: [HTTP/1.1] Response header cap counts decoded line characters only and has no field-count limit
body:
## Summary
The parser adds line.Length (no CRLF, no status line) to a 102400 byte cap, so 51,200 two-byte field lines (about 200 KB on the wire) pass, each allocating strings, a tuple and a header entry. With up to 10 interim 1xx heads plus the final one, a hostile server can force about half a million small allocations per request on a mobile device. ConnectReplyReader, by contrast, charges every byte.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:292`

## Problem
ParseNextHeadDataAsync adds line.Length (without CRLF, without the status line) to totalHeaderBytes and compares with MaxTotalHeaderBytes = 102400 (Http11ResponseParser.cs:158, 292-294). A minimal field 'a:' counts 2, so 51,200 field lines (204,800 wire bytes) pass; each allocates a name string, a value string, a tuple in the pooled scratch list (which keeps its grown capacity) and an HttpHeaders entry (297-302). The loop can repeat for up to 10 interim 1xx heads plus the final one (242-254). ConnectReplyReader, by contrast, charges every byte (ConnectReplyReader.cs:355).

**Failure scenario.** A hostile server answers every request with 10 interim responses and a final one, each carrying 51,200 two-byte fields: roughly 2 MB on the wire turns into about half a million small allocations and tens of MB of transient managed memory per request on a mobile device, plus 16 pooled scratch lists pinned at their grown capacity.

## Suggested fix
Charge line.Length + 2 (and the status line) against the byte cap and add an explicit field-count cap (a few hundred) per head; consider a combined budget across interim heads.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each header line is charged line length plus 2 (and the status line) against the byte cap, and a per-head field-count cap is enforced
- [ ] A combined budget applies across interim heads, or the limit is documented per head
- [ ] An over-limit head fails with a bounded-size error without further allocation
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it with 51,200 minimal fields and with many interim responses

title: [HTTP/1.1] The response parser's line API returns strings, forcing per-line Latin-1 strings and an intermediate scratch list
body:
## Summary
ReadLineAsync returns Task<string>, ParseResponseHeaderLine allocates name and value strings, stores them in a scratch list and copies that list into HttpHeaders. Trailer readers and the CONNECT drain reuse the string API. A byte/span line API, as ReadChunkSizeAsync already uses, would remove the strings, the scratch hop and the second chunk-size parser.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:296`

## Problem
ReadLineAsync returns Task<string> (:1139, decode at :1532); ParseResponseHeaderLine then allocates name and value strings (:721-722), stores them in a pooled scratch list (:297) and immediately copies the list into a new HttpHeaders (:300-302). The trailer readers (:924-941; Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:409-430) and the CONNECT drain reuse the string API. #120 item 19c.2 tracks the allocations; the design point is that a byte/span line API (ReadChunkSizeAsync already works that way) would also remove the scratch-list hop and the second chunk-size parser.

**Failure scenario.** Three strings and a Task<string> per header line on every response head.

## Suggested fix
When doing #120, change the reader to expose the line as bytes in its buffer and add fields straight to HttpHeaders.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The reader exposes a header line as bytes in its buffer and fields are added straight to HttpHeaders
- [ ] Per-header-line allocations (strings, Task<string>, scratch tuple) are removed; the target is recorded as allocations per response head before and after
- [ ] Trailer and CONNECT paths use the same line API or are explicitly left as is
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it confirming identical parsed headers

title: [HTTP/1.1] An HTTP/1.0 response with Transfer-Encoding: chunked is delivered as raw chunk framing read until close
body:
## Summary
DetermineBodyKind returns ReadToEnd for any HTTP/1.0 response with a Transfer-Encoding header before classifying the coding, and the header remains in the delivered headers. RFC 9112 Section 6.3 still applies chunked as the final coding. A server or old proxy that labels a chunked reply HTTP/1.0 gives the application a body containing hex sizes and CRLFs, and the read can hang until timeout if the peer keeps the connection open.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:486`

## Problem
DetermineBodyKind returns ReadToEnd for isHttp10 && hasTransferEncoding before the coding is even classified (Http11ResponseParser.cs:486-493); the Transfer-Encoding header stays in the delivered headers. Test Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:196 (ParseHead_Http10WithTransferEncoding_ReadsToCloseAndIsNotReused) pins it. RFC 9112 Section 6.1 only says the framing must be treated as faulty and the connection closed after processing; the body length rule that still applies is Section 6.3 item 4 (chunked final coding: decode until the coding says the data is complete).

**Failure scenario.** A server or old proxy labels a chunked reply 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK'. The application gets status 200 and a body of '1a<CR><LF>...0<CR><LF><CR><LF>' (hex sizes and CRLFs inside the payload), and if the peer keeps the connection open after the last chunk the read hangs until the request timeout.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 6.1, 6.3

## Suggested fix
Classify the coding first: when it is exactly chunked, decode it (Chunked body kind) and force KeepAlive=false; keep ReadToEnd only for non-chunked/unknown codings, or fail the response. Update the test accordingly.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the final transfer coding is exactly chunked, the body is decoded as chunked and the connection is not reused (KeepAlive false)
- [ ] ReadToEnd is kept only for non-chunked or unknown codings, or those responses fail with a defined error
- [ ] Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.ParseHead_Http10WithTransferEncoding_ReadsToCloseAndIsNotReused is updated to the new behavior
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it for an HTTP/1.0 chunked response

title: [HTTP/1.1] Parser exceptions echo peer-controlled status-line and chunk-size bytes into error messages and logs
body:
## Summary
ParseStatusLine and ParseChunkSizeToken put the raw status code span (up to 8 KB) or chunk-size token (up to 256 bytes) into the FormatException message. That text is copied into UHttpError.Message and reaches the Unity console, crash reporters and the HTTP monitor. The header-line path already avoids echoing the line, so the behaviour is inconsistent.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:689`

## Problem
ParseStatusLine throws FormatException('Invalid HTTP status code: ' + statusCodeSpan) (Http11ResponseParser.cs:689) where the span is everything between the first and second space of a line that may be 8192 characters long; ParseChunkSizeToken echoes the token in both overloads (805, 808, 826, 829; up to 256 bytes). MapDispatchAttemptFailure and the body source copy the text into UHttpError.Message ('Malformed HTTP response: ...', RawSocketTransport.cs:809-813, Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:171-174). The header-line path was deliberately written not to echo ('Messages never echo the line', 696).

**Failure scenario.** A server replies 'HTTP/1.1 ' followed by 8 KB of control characters, ANSI escapes or fake log lines without a space. The text lands verbatim in the exception message, the Unity console, crash reporters and the HTTP monitor (log forging, oversized log entries).

## Suggested fix
Use fixed messages ('Invalid HTTP status code', 'Invalid chunk size') as the header-line path does; if a diagnostic value is wanted, include at most a short, hex-escaped prefix.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] ParseStatusLine and both ParseChunkSizeToken overloads throw FormatException with fixed messages ('Invalid HTTP status code', 'Invalid chunk size') that contain no peer bytes, or at most a short hex-escaped prefix
- [ ] UHttpError.Message for a malformed status line or chunk size contains no raw control characters from the response
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it (status line with 8 KB of control characters, malformed chunk-size token)
