title: [HTTP/1.1] obs-fold in a response header is rejected with NetworkError although a user agent MUST replace it with SP (RFC 9112 5.2)
body:
## Summary
Http11ResponseParser throws FormatException for any field line starting with SP or HTAB, so the whole response fails as 'Malformed HTTP response'. RFC 9112 Section 5.2 only allows rejection for servers and proxies; a user agent must replace each obs-fold with one or more SP. Legacy servers and gateways that fold long fields (Digest challenges, Set-Cookie, CSP) are unreachable, and existing tests pin the non-conformant behaviour.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:701`

## Problem
ParseResponseHeaderLine throws FormatException('Obsolete line folding (obs-fold) in response headers is not supported') for every field line that starts with SP/HTAB (Http11ResponseParser.cs:701-702), which MapDispatchAttemptFailure turns into NetworkError 'Malformed HTTP response' (RawSocketTransport.cs:809-813). Tests assert it: Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:242 (Parse_ObsFoldContinuationLine_ThrowsFormatException) and :249. The decision came from closed issue #41, whose text reads the RFC as 'replace with SP or reject'; RFC 9112 Section 5.2 gives the reject option only to servers (400) and proxies/gateways (502). For a user agent the sentence is: 'A user agent that receives an obs-fold in a response message that is not within a message/http container MUST replace each received obs-fold with one or more SP octets prior to interpreting the field value.'

**Failure scenario.** A legacy server, appliance or CGI gateway folds a long field ('WWW-Authenticate: Digest realm=x, CRLF SP nonce=y', long Set-Cookie or CSP). Every response from that origin fails with NetworkError although browsers and curl accept it.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 5.2

## Suggested fix
When a line starts with SP/HTAB and a previous field exists, append SP + the trimmed continuation to that field's value (never create a new field, so the #41 smuggling concern stays closed); keep rejecting a whitespace-led line directly after the status line (RFC 9112 Section 2.2). Replace the two tests with unfolding assertions, including a folded Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding case.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A response header line starting with SP/HTAB after an existing field is appended to that field's value as SP plus the trimmed continuation, and never creates a new field
- [ ] A whitespace-led line directly after the status line is still rejected (RFC 9112 Section 2.2)
- [ ] A folded Content-Length or Transfer-Encoding value is unfolded before framing decisions are taken
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it; Parse_ObsFoldContinuationLine_ThrowsFormatException and its sibling are replaced with unfolding assertions

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: ParseResponseHeaderLine throws on any SP/HTAB-led field line (Http11ResponseParser.cs:701-702), mapped to NetworkError 'Malformed HTTP response' (RawSocketTransport.cs:809-813), pinned by Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:242-253. The decision came from closed #41, whose text reads RFC 9112 Section 5.2 as 'replace with SP or reject'; the reject option there is for servers and proxies, a user agent MUST replace the obs-fold with SP. So the documented trade-off rests on a wrong reading and the finding holds as an RFC deviation. Lowered to low: the reject is a deliberate hardening against the framing ambiguity #41 fixed, obs-fold from live servers is rare, and the failure is a clean error, not a mis-parse.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Response header values containing NUL, bare CR or other C0 controls are delivered to the application unchanged
body:
## Summary
ParseResponseHeaderLine validates the header name but copies the value without any octet check, and HttpHeaders.Add does not check either. Trailer values with CR are already rejected and ConnectReplyReader replaces bare CR, so the paths disagree. A hostile origin can inject NUL or CR into values that reach cookies, redirects, logs and native plugins, and a stored value that is later sent back makes HttpFieldValidator reject every such request.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:722`

## Problem
ReadLineAsync splits on LF only and DecodeLineFromBuffer strips at most one trailing CR (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1515-1533), so 'X: a<CR>b<CR><LF>' yields the line 'X: a<CR>b'. ParseResponseHeaderLine validates the name but copies the value as is (722) and HttpHeaders.Add performs no value check (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:49-64). NUL and every other C0 control pass the same way. The code is inconsistent with itself: trailer values with CR are rejected (ValidateHeaderValue, 949-953) and ConnectReplyReader replaces a bare CR with SP (ConnectReplyReader.cs:360-370).

**Failure scenario.** A hostile or compromised origin returns 'Set-Cookie: id=1<CR>...' , 'Location: /x<NUL>y' or 'X-Request-Id: a<CR>FAKE LOG LINE'. The value reaches cookie storage, redirect handling, the HTTP monitor, loggers and any native plugin the game hands it to: NUL truncates C strings, bare CR forges lines in logs/Editor console, and a stored value that later goes back out in a request header makes the serializer's HttpFieldValidator reject every such request (InvalidRequest) until the state is cleared.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 5.5; RFC 9112 Section 2.2

## Suggested fix
In ParseResponseHeaderLine reject the message (FormatException, as for the other field-line errors) or replace each CR/NUL with SP, and reject remaining C0 controls except HTAB and DEL; apply the same rule to trailers so both paths agree. Add strictness tests for bare CR and NUL inside a value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Response header values with NUL, bare CR or other C0 controls (except HTAB) and DEL are rejected with FormatException (mapped to NetworkError) or have CR/NUL replaced with SP, one rule documented and applied
- [ ] Trailer values follow the same rule as header values
- [ ] Strictness tests cover bare CR and NUL inside a header value and inside a trailer value
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ReadLineAsync splits on LF only (IndexOfLf 1341-1350) and DecodeLineFromBuffer strips one trailing CR (1521-1524), so an interior bare CR or NUL stays in the line. ParseResponseHeaderLine validates the name only and copies the trimmed value (Http11ResponseParser.cs:715-722); HttpHeaders.Add does no value check (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:49-64). The trailer path does reject CR/LF (ValidateHeaderValue 949-953 via AddResponseTrailer 752), so the two paths disagree. RFC 9110 Section 5.5: a recipient of CR, LF or NUL in a field value MUST reject the message or replace each with SP. Interior NUL and other C0 controls are not whitespace and are never trimmed, so they reach the application, cookie storage and logs unchanged.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Received header, trailer and HTTP/2 fields are validated by three unrelated routines that accept different inputs
body:
## Summary
Outgoing fields share HttpFieldValidator, but incoming fields do not: HTTP/1.1 headers check only the name, HTTP/1.1 trailers use a lenient parser that trims names and drops prohibited fields yet throws on CR in values, and HTTP/2 applies its own rules. The same origin therefore gets different results per protocol (a trailer 'content-length' is returned over HTTP/2 and dropped over HTTP/1.1).

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:741`

## Problem
Outgoing fields share one validator (HttpFieldValidator, called from Http11RequestSerializer.cs:517-518 and Http2Connection.Send.cs:457, 472). Incoming fields do not: (1) ParseResponseHeaderLine (Http11ResponseParser.cs:698-723) checks that the name is a token and does nothing to the value; (2) AddResponseTrailer (:741-759) uses a different, lenient line parser (TryParseHeaderLine :725-739 trims the name, so 'X-A : v' is accepted as a trailer but rejected as a header), silently drops bad names and TrailerFieldValidator-prohibited names, yet throws FormatException for a CR in the value (:752, 949-953), which fails the whole response although the comments at :939-940 and Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:428-429 say invalid trailers are skipped/ignored (Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:227 pins the throw); (3) HTTP/2 GetMalformedResponseFieldReason (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:757-787) rejects NUL/CR/LF and leading/trailing SP/HT in values with a stream error, and HTTP/2 trailers (:694 stream.AppendTrailers) never pass through TrailerFieldValidator.IsProhibitedResponseTrailer, whose only caller is Http11ResponseParser.cs:754. TrailerFieldValidator and HttpFieldValidator sit in Transport/Internal, but there is no counterpart for received fields.

**Failure scenario.** The same origin answering over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2: a trailer 'content-length: 5' or 'authorization: x' is returned by GetTrailersAsync on HTTP/2 and dropped on HTTP/1.1; a field value containing NUL or a bare CR is a stream error on HTTP/2, accepted verbatim as an HTTP/1.1 header and a fatal 'Malformed HTTP response' as an HTTP/1.1 trailer. Code that consumes trailers (status trailers, cache commit) behaves differently per negotiated protocol.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 5.5 and 6.5.1; RFC 9113 Section 8.2.1

## Suggested fix
Introduce one internal ResponseFieldValidator in Transport/Internal (name token, value octet rules, prohibited-trailer policy returning Accept / Drop / Reject) and call it from the HTTP/1.1 header path, the HTTP/1.1 trailer path and the HTTP/2 header and trailer paths; decide drop-versus-reject once and correct the comments.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One internal ResponseFieldValidator in Transport/Internal defines name token rules, value octet rules and the prohibited-trailer policy (Accept / Drop / Reject)
- [ ] The HTTP/1.1 header path, HTTP/1.1 trailer path and HTTP/2 header and trailer paths all call it
- [ ] Drop-versus-reject is decided once and the comments in Http11ResponseParser and Http11ResponseBodySource are corrected
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it covering the same field input across HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced all three paths. (1) HTTP/1.1 headers: ParseResponseHeaderLine (Http11ResponseParser.cs:698-723) validates only the name; the line reader splits on LF only and DecodeLineFromBuffer strips just the terminating CR/LF (:1515-1533), so a bare CR or NUL inside a field value reaches HttpHeaders verbatim. RFC 9110 Section 5.5 requires reject-or-replace for CR/LF/NUL, so this is a real gap, not only an inconsistency. (2) HTTP/1.1 trailers: AddResponseTrailer (:741-759) uses the lenient TryParseHeaderLine (:725-739, trims the name so 'X-A : v' passes), silently drops bad and prohibited names, but ValidateHeaderValue (:949-953) throws FormatException for CR, failing the whole response; the comments at :939-940 and Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:428-429 say such trailers are skipped. The throw is pinned by tests (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:227-235; the cited path Tests/.../Http1/Http11ResponseParserTests.cs does not exist, the file is one directory up) and Http11ResponseBodySourceTests.cs:168. (3) HTTP/2: GetMalformedResponseFieldReason (Http2Connection.ReadLoop.cs:757-787) rejects NUL/CR/LF and edge whitespace with a stream error, and trailers go straight to stream.AppendTrailers (:694 -> Http2Stream.cs:452-455 -> SetTrailers) with no prohibited-name filter; TrailerFieldValidator.IsProhibitedResponseTrailer has a single caller (Http11ResponseParser.cs:754). No shared received-field validator exists in Transport/Internal. The H2 trailer difference itself is harmless under RFC 9110 Section 6.5.1 (trailers are kept separate from headers), so medium rests on the H1 header-value gap and the protocol-dependent behaviour. No open issue tracks it.

Related: [[R11-http1-protocol-07]], [[R11-http1-protocol-06]].

title: [HTTP/1.1] Comma-list and whitespace handling is duplicated in six scanners and three trim helpers with three whitespace definitions
body:
## Summary
Http11ResponseParser, ExpectContinueHelper and ConnectReplyReader each have their own list scanner and trim helper (char.IsWhiteSpace, string.Trim, SP/HT/CR/LF). They already disagree: ConnectReplyReader looks at one Connection line while the parser walks all field lines. Every new header rule has to be fixed in up to six places.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:777`

## Problem
Trim helpers: Http11ResponseParser.TrimWhitespace (:777-793, char.IsWhiteSpace), ExpectContinueHelper.TrimWhitespace (Runtime/Transport/Internal/ExpectContinueHelper.cs:125-138, a copy), string.Trim() in ConnectReplyReader (:130, 270, 292, 303) and in TryGetValidatedContentLength (:578, 583), plus a byte-level IsAsciiWhitespace (:1574-1580: SP/HT/CR/LF). List scanners: ClassifyTransferEncoding (:535-564), IsKeepAlive (:598-644), ExpectContinueHelper.HeaderValueContainsToken (:101-123) and HasOnlyExpectContinueExpectation (:69-99), ConnectReplyReader.ContainsToken (:295-308, allocating via Split) and EndsWithChunked (:285-293). They already disagree: the parser walks every field line (GetValues) while ConnectReply.HasConnectionClose / CanRetryOnSameConnection / DrainBodyCoreAsync read only the first line (Headers.Get at ConnectReplyReader.cs:44, 59-61, 163, 180; HttpHeaders.Get returns values[0], Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:70-75); EndsWithChunked accepts 'gzip, chunked' where ClassifyTransferEncoding rejects it; and none uses RFC 9110 OWS (SP / HTAB): char.IsWhiteSpace also matches U+0085 and U+00A0, which are obs-text bytes after Latin-1 decoding (the behavioural effect on field values at :722 is reported by the protocol lens). Core offers no shared helper; WebSocketHandshakeValidator.ContainsToken (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:472) and DecompressionHandler (:752) are further copies outside the slice.

**Failure scenario.** A proxy answers CONNECT with 407 and two field lines 'Connection: keep-alive' then 'Connection: close' (or two different Content-Length lines): ConnectReply.CanRetryOnSameConnection is true from the first line, the authenticated CONNECT is written to a connection the proxy closes (or after a mis-sized drain) and the request fails with NetworkError instead of reconnecting; the same header block given to Http11ResponseParser yields KeepAlive=false or 'Conflicting Content-Length values'. Every new header rule has to be fixed in up to six scanners.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 5.5, 5.6.1, 5.6.3

## Suggested fix
Add one allocation-free field-list tokenizer and one TrimOws (SP/HTAB only) in TurboHTTP.Core.Internal, span based and iterating all field lines, and replace the six scanners and three trim helpers with it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One allocation-free, span-based field-list tokenizer and one TrimOws (SP/HTAB only) exist in TurboHTTP.Core.Internal and iterate all field lines
- [ ] The six scanners and three trim helpers are replaced by them, and ConnectReplyReader.ContainsToken no longer allocates through Split
- [ ] A CONNECT reply with 'Connection: keep-alive' followed by 'Connection: close' yields CanRetryOnSameConnection false, and conflicting Content-Length lines are rejected as in the parser
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described. Trim copies: Http11ResponseParser.TrimWhitespace (Http11ResponseParser.cs:777-793, char.IsWhiteSpace) and ExpectContinueHelper.TrimWhitespace (ExpectContinueHelper.cs:125-138); string.Trim() at ConnectReplyReader.cs:130/270/292/303 and Http11ResponseParser.cs:578/583; byte-level IsAsciiWhitespace at :1574-1580. List scanners: ClassifyTransferEncoding :535-564, IsKeepAlive :598-644, ExpectContinueHelper :69-99 and :101-123, ConnectReplyReader.ContainsToken :295-308 (Split allocates) and EndsWithChunked :285-293; further copies at WebSocketHandshakeValidator.cs:472 and DecompressionHandler.cs:~752. The divergence is real: ConnectReply.HasConnectionClose / CanRetryOnSameConnection (ConnectReplyReader.cs:44, 57-61) and DrainBodyCoreAsync (:163, :180) use HttpHeaders.Get, which returns values[0] (HttpHeaders.cs:70-75), while the main parser iterates GetValues. Traced scenario: 407 with 'Connection: keep-alive' then 'Connection: close' plus Content-Length gives CanRetryOnSameConnection=true, so RawSocketTransport.cs:1481-1488 drains and re-sends CONNECT on the same stream instead of returning null to reconnect; the next ReadAsync fails with NetworkError. No guard found. Severity lowered: the failure needs a proxy that splits contradictory Connection/Content-Length values over two field lines (legal but rare); the EndsWithChunked vs ClassifyTransferEncoding difference is benign because the drain only needs the framing (final coding chunked), and the HTTP path never drains a TE reply (CanRetryOnSameConnection requires TE == null, :59). The rest is duplication/maintainability. No open issue tracks it.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Header values and framing tokens are trimmed with char.IsWhiteSpace, stripping bytes 0x85/0xA0 and accepting VT/FF/CR
body:
## Summary
TrimWhitespace uses char.IsWhiteSpace on Latin-1 decoded lines, so a trailing 0x85 or 0xA0 byte (common as the last byte of UTF-8 text) is removed from values, and VT, FF and CR are treated as optional whitespace. RFC 9110 Section 5.6.3 defines OWS as SP/HTAB only. This corrupts redirect targets and filenames and accepts 'Content-Length: <VT>42' or 'Transfer-Encoding: <FF>chunked', the kind of disagreement response smuggling uses.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:777`

## Problem
TrimWhitespace (Http11ResponseParser.cs:777-793) uses char.IsWhiteSpace. Lines are decoded as Latin-1 (DecodeLineFromBuffer, 1532), so bytes 0x85 and 0xA0 become U+0085/U+00A0, both whitespace for char.IsWhiteSpace, as are 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x0D. It is applied to every header value (722), trailer names and values (736-737), the status code (686), Transfer-Encoding and Connection tokens (544, 613-614), and Content-Length is trimmed again with string.Trim() (578, 583). RFC 9110 Section 5.6.3 defines OWS as SP / HTAB only and Section 5.5 makes 0x80-0xFF (obs-text) part of the value.

**Failure scenario.** (1) Data corruption: a server sends a raw UTF-8 value whose last byte is 0xA0 or 0x85, e.g. 'Location: /caf/voil' + C3 A0 (a-grave) or a Content-Disposition filename ending in Cyrillic 'kha' (D1 85). The final byte is stripped, so the redirect target or filename the application sees is a different, invalid byte sequence. (2) Lenient framing: 'Content-Length: <VT>42' and 'Transfer-Encoding: <FF>chunked' are accepted as 42/chunked although a conforming intermediary treats them as invalid or as an unknown coding, which is the disagreement response-smuggling relies on.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 5.5, 5.6.3; RFC 9112 Section 6.3

## Suggested fix
Trim only SP and HTAB (one shared helper for the parser, the trailer path and ExpectContinueHelper), and parse Content-Length from the already-trimmed value without string.Trim(). Add tests for a value ending in 0xA0/0x85 (must be preserved) and for VT/FF around Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding (must be rejected).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Header, trailer, status-code and framing-token trimming removes only SP and HTAB, using one shared helper also used by ExpectContinueHelper
- [ ] Content-Length is parsed from the already-trimmed value without string.Trim()
- [ ] A value ending in 0xA0 or 0x85 is preserved; VT/FF around Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding is rejected
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. TrimWhitespace uses char.IsWhiteSpace (Http11ResponseParser.cs:777-793); lines are decoded as Latin-1 (1532), so bytes 0x85/0xA0 become U+0085/U+00A0, both whitespace, as are VT/FF/CR. It is applied to every header value (722), trailer name/value (736-737), status code (686), Transfer-Encoding tokens (544) and Connection tokens (613-614); Content-Length is trimmed again with string.Trim() before long.TryParse(NumberStyles.None) (578, 583). Result: a raw UTF-8 value whose last byte is 0xA0 or 0x85 loses that byte, and 'Content-Length: <VT>42' / 'Transfer-Encoding: <FF>chunked' are accepted although RFC 9110 Section 5.6.3 limits OWS to SP/HTAB. No guard downstream (HttpHeaders.Add stores the value as given, Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:49-64). The chunk-size path already uses an ASCII-only helper (IsAsciiWhitespace 1574-1580), so the header path is the inconsistent one.

Related: [[R11-http1-design-03]], [[R11-http1-protocol-07]].

title: [HTTP/1.1] Abort()/Dispose during a pending body read returns the reader's pooled buffers while the socket read still targets them
body:
## Summary
Http11ResponseBodySource documents that reads and abort are serialized by the caller, but UHttpStreamingResponse.Dispose and ResponseBodyStream.Dispose call Abort without checking for an in-flight ReadAsync. CloseBody disposes the BufferedStreamReader, which returns its buffers to ArrayPool.Shared unless a raced read is pending; a non-cancellable pending read is not tracked. Bytes arriving after the return are written into an array another consumer may already hold, so data of one response can land in another.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1100`

## Problem
Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:12-13 states that reads and disposal/abort are 'expected to be serialized by the caller', but the only caller does not serialize: UHttpStreamingResponse.Dispose -> StartBodyDispose calls _bodySource.Abort() whenever EOF was not reached (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:157-159), ResponseBodyStream.Dispose -> AbortBody (ResponseBodyStream.cs:180-186, UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:142-147); neither checks for an in-flight ReadAsync. Abort -> CloseBody (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:254-258, 676-684) calls _reader.Dispose() BEFORE _lease.Dispose(). BufferedStreamReader.Dispose (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1090-1111) keeps buffers out of the pool only when _raceRead is pending or _bodyReadState != Idle. A body-phase read whose token cannot be cancelled never leaves Idle: ReadBodyAsync returns 'new ValueTask<int>(pending)' at 1415-1417 without touching _bodyReadState. In streaming mode the transport token is CancellationToken.None (RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830), so a consumer that reads with no token (ResponseBodyStream.Read passes CancellationToken.None at ResponseBodyStream.cs:62; ReadAsync(buffer) / CopyToAsync default token) takes this path. Every chunk-size line, chunk CRLF, trailer line and every read with a destination below 4096 bytes goes through FillBufferAsync into the reader's _buffer (1364-1376). So Dispose runs ByteArrayPool.Return(_buffer) at 1108 while _stream.ReadAsync(_buffer, ...) is still pending. For a raced (cancellable) pending read the buffers are abandoned correctly, but Abort does not complete the pending ValueTask: only the read's own completion or the token does (1431-1502). architecture.md lists this contract explicitly ('Never return a buffer while an OS operation or another thread may still touch it ... HTTP/2 abort vs read').

**Failure scenario.** Unity app streams a chunked response (SSE or a chunked download) on a background continuation with 'await stream.ReadAsync(buf)' (no token); the main thread calls response.Dispose() in OnDestroy while the read is pending in a chunk-size/CRLF refill. Abort returns the 4 KB _buffer to ArrayPool.Shared and only then shuts the socket down. Bytes that were already queued in the kernel (data arriving in the same instant, which is the normal state of an active download) are still delivered to the pending recv after shutdown and are written into an array the pool can hand out again at once (the next BufferedStreamReader on that thread rents the same 4096 bucket): bytes of one response land in another request's header/body buffer. Independently, the pending read is completed only if the platform ends it; the code base documents that IL2CPP does not always do that after shutdown/close (#293, #384: 53 of 600 abandons on the iOS simulator), in which case the consumer's ReadAsync task never completes when it has no token.

## Suggested fix
Make the reader own an in-flight flag for every body-phase stream read (not only raced ones) and abandon the buffers in Dispose whenever a read is in flight. Arm the existing IValueTaskSource race for non-cancellable reads too, and let CloseBody/Abort win it (CAS Pending->Abandoned, fail the pending read with ObjectDisposedException) instead of relying on the socket to end the read. Add a test with AbandonedReadStream: Abort during a pending CancellationToken.None read must complete the read and must not return the read target to the pool.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The reader tracks an in-flight flag for every body-phase stream read, not only raced ones, and Dispose abandons (does not return) the buffers while a read is in flight
- [ ] Abort/CloseBody win the race for a pending non-cancellable read (Pending to Abandoned) and fail it with ObjectDisposedException
- [ ] Pooled buffers are returned exactly once on every path: completion, exception, cancellation, dispose
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it using AbandonedReadStream: Abort during a pending CancellationToken.None read completes the read and never returns the read target to the pool

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-runtime-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: high. Angle: concurrency.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Core does not serialise abort against reads: UHttpStreamingResponse.Dispose -> StartBodyDispose calls _bodySource.Abort() whenever EOF was not reached (Runtime/Core/UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:155-160), ResponseBodyStream dispose -> AbortBody (ResponseBodyStream.cs:180-186; UHttpStreamingResponse.cs:142-148). Streaming mode passes CancellationToken.None as the transport token (RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830) and ResponseBodyStream.Read passes None (ResponseBodyStream.cs:62), so GetEffectiveReadToken returns a non-cancellable token (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:640-641). Every chunk-size/CRLF/trailer read and every read with a destination under 4096 bytes goes FillBufferAsync -> ReadBodyAsync(_buffer) (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1364-1376), which returns 'new ValueTask<int>(pending)' at 1415-1417 without leaving BodyReadIdle. CloseBody then runs _reader.Dispose() before _lease.Dispose() (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:676-684) and Dispose returns _buffer to the shared pool because _raceRead is null and the state is Idle (1099-1110), while the stream read still targets it. HoldingNetworkStream deliberately lets a read pending under dispose end later (Tcp/HoldingNetworkStream.cs:12-17), so the read can still complete with data into a pooled array; this breaks the rule in architecture.md:109-110. The window for another renter to be hit is narrow, and the 'read never completes without a token' part depends on the platform (#293/#384 behaviour), but the ownership violation itself is static. No test aborts during a pending non-cancellable body read.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Head parse allocates a Task<string> and three strings per header line
body:
## Summary
ReadLineAsync is an async Task<string>, each line is decoded to a string, then ParseResponseHeaderLine makes separate name and value strings, and HttpHeaders.Add allocates a List<string> per name. A 15-header response produces about 2-3 KB of garbage on the default path. #120 item 19c.2 only names Substring/Split, which are already gone.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1139`

## Problem
ReadLineAsync is 'async Task<string>' (1139): one Task<string> per line even when the line is already buffered. Each line is Latin-1 decoded into a string (1532), then ParseResponseHeaderLine makes a name string and a value string with ToString (721-722) and the line string is dropped. HttpHeaders.Add then allocates a List<string> per name (Runtime/Core/HttpHeaders.cs:62). Substring/Split are already gone, so the remaining cost is not what #120 item 19c.2 describes.

**Failure scenario.** A response with 15 header lines: about 16 Task<string>, 16 line strings and 30 name/value strings, roughly 2-3 KB of garbage per response on the default request path.

## Suggested fix
Parse name and value straight from the byte buffer (status line and header lines as spans, a synchronous TryReadLine fast path with an async refill only when no LF is buffered), intern well-known header names, and decode only the value.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Status line and header lines are parsed from the byte buffer as spans with a synchronous fast path when a full line is buffered
- [ ] Well-known header names are interned and only values are decoded to strings
- [ ] Allocation per 15-header response is reduced to the name/value strings plus the header list, measured by an allocation test with a stated byte budget
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context

title: [HTTP/1.1] Http11ResponseParser.cs mixes three head DTOs, a reader mode switch hidden in a constructor and two copy-pasted line readers
body:
## Summary
ParsedResponseHeadData, ParsedResponseHead and ParsedResponse carry the same values, and constructing a ParsedResponseHead silently switches the reader from head-phase to body-phase reads. The 570-line BufferedStreamReader is nested in a static parser class, and the text-line and chunk-size line readers duplicate logic with different end-of-stream rules, so the same truncation is reported differently depending on the byte.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1208`

## Problem
ParsedResponseHeadData (struct, :164-189), ParsedResponseHead (class, :110-149) and ParsedResponse (:21-100) carry the same five values; the head is copied field by field (:343-350). Constructing a ParsedResponseHead calls reader.MarkHeadComplete() (:117), which silently switches the reader from head-phase reads (AbandonableTask race, :1379-1393) to body-phase reads (IValueTaskSource race, :1370-1376): an ordering contract enforced only by where a DTO is constructed (the fuzz target relies on it, Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:111). The 570-line BufferedStreamReader with its abandon/race machinery is a nested class of a static parser (:1038-1608) although RawSocketTransport constructs it and the body source owns it. ReadLineAsync (:1139-1206) and ReadChunkSizeAsync (:1208-1268) are the same 60-line accumulate loop; they differ in that end of stream inside a line is an IOException in the first (:1194) and is parsed as a complete chunk-size line in the second (:1259), and end of stream before any byte is null in one and FormatException 'Invalid chunk size: empty' in the other (:1257). There are two chunk-size token parsers (char :795-814, byte :816-835) and two chunk-line strippers (:761-775, 1535-1572) with different whitespace sets. StatusCode is typed System.Net.HttpStatusCode and cast back to int at every use (:247; RawSocketTransport.cs:1663, 1712, 1890, 2247, 2271). DetermineBodyKind (:439-521) also mutates the header collection and records a diagnostics event.

**Failure scenario.** A truncated chunked body is reported as 'Malformed HTTP response: Invalid chunk size: empty' or as an unexpected-end IOException depending on which byte the cut falls on, and a later change to line reading (limit, terminator rule) has to be made in both loops; a new caller that reads a body through a reader for which no head object was constructed gets head-phase read semantics without any error.

## Suggested fix
Move BufferedStreamReader to its own file with an explicit BeginBody() transition, keep one line-accumulation routine that yields a byte span for both the text-line and chunk-size callers, keep one head type with an int status, and make DetermineBodyKind pure (return the framing decision and let the caller edit headers).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] BufferedStreamReader lives in its own file with an explicit BeginBody() transition instead of a constructor side effect (the fuzz target in Tools~/fuzz is updated)
- [ ] One line-accumulation routine serves both the text-line and chunk-size callers with a single end-of-stream rule
- [ ] One head type remains, and DetermineBodyKind is pure
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it showing a truncated chunked body yields the same error regardless of the cut position

## Context

title: [HTTP/1.1] The reader-owned body buffer is sized by the first large read and caps every later socket read for that response
body:
## Summary
For cancellable body reads the BufferedStreamReader rents _bodyBuffer sized by the first qualifying destination and never re-rents it. The body source clamps destinations to the bytes left in a chunk, so the first qualifying read is often small and every later read is capped at that size, multiplying socket reads, async transitions and token registrations (16x for a 4096-byte first read).

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1320`

## Problem
ReadAsync(Memory) for a cancellable body read with destination.Length >= _buffer.Length (4096) does '_bodyBuffer ??= ByteArrayPool.Rent(Math.Min(destination.Length, MaxBodyReadBufferBytes))' and then reads at most 'Math.Min(destination.Length, bodyBuffer.Length)' (1320-1325). _bodyBuffer is never re-rented, so its size is fixed by whichever read first qualified. The body source clamps the destination to the bytes left in the current chunk or body (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:325-326, 343-344), so the first qualifying read is often small. The journal (2026-11-cancel-reads.md, 'rented once per body, at most 64 KiB') does not mention the first-read sizing.

**Failure scenario.** Streaming download read with a 64 KB buffer and a cancellable token. (a) Chunked response whose first chunk has 4-8 KB left after the head buffer is consumed, followed by large chunks: _bodyBuffer becomes 8192 and every following read returns at most 8 KB, eight times the socket reads, async transitions and token registrations of the intended 64 KB reads. (b) Consumer reads a 4096-byte file header first and then the bulk with a large buffer: every read of the remaining body is capped at 4096 bytes (16x the reads; for a 100 MB body about 24000 extra read round trips, each with a registration on a pending read).

## Suggested fix
Rent _bodyBuffer at MaxBodyReadBufferBytes (or the configured streaming receive size) regardless of the first destination, or re-rent a larger one when a later destination exceeds it and no read is pending.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] _bodyBuffer is rented at MaxBodyReadBufferBytes (or the configured streaming receive size), or re-rented larger when no read is pending
- [ ] A 64 KB cancellable read after a small first read returns up to 64 KB per socket read
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it counting socket reads for a chunked response whose first chunk is small
- [ ] Pooled buffer is still returned once on every path

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-runtime-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Code is as described: '_bodyBuffer ??= ByteArrayPool.Rent(Math.Min(destination.Length, MaxBodyReadBufferBytes))' and the read is capped at Math.Min(destination.Length, bodyBuffer.Length) (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1320-1325); _bodyBuffer is never re-rented. The body source clamps the destination to the bytes left in the chunk/body (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:325-326, 343-344), so a first qualifying read of 4096-8191 bytes fixes the cap at 4-8 KB (ArrayPool rounds up to a power of two) for the rest of the response. The path is taken for every read with a cancellable token, which includes all buffered responses (transport token = request token, RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830). Lowered to low: no correctness impact, the extra reads are unmeasured, and Content-Length bodies normally start with a full-size read; the realistic case is a chunked body whose first chunk remainder is small and later chunks are large.

title: [HTTP/1.1] Every reader refill allocates: FillBufferAsync is an async Task<int> over the Task-returning Stream.ReadAsync overload
body:
## Summary
FillBufferAsync allocates a Task<int> per call and the reader reads through Stream.ReadAsync(byte[],int,int,CancellationToken), which allocates a second Task<int> per socket read; SaeaStream and PollSelectStream implement it as AsTask() over a ValueTask. This sits under chunk-size, CRLF, trailer and small body reads and is a candidate root cause of the per-read allocations measured in #434.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1364`

## Problem
FillBufferAsync is declared 'private async Task<int>' (1364): a Task<int> is allocated per call even when the inner read completes synchronously (results outside the builder's small-int cache). It sits under every body read with a destination below 4096 bytes and under every chunk-size/CRLF/trailer read. Both body-phase and head-phase reads use Stream.ReadAsync(byte[], int, int, CancellationToken) (1379, 1415), so the stream allocates a second Task<int> per socket read; for the SAEA and PollSelect modes that overload is literally '.AsTask()' over the channel's ValueTask (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/SaeaStream.cs:53-56, PollSelectStream.cs:49-52), which defeats the mode ConnectionPoolOptions documents as zero-allocation socket I/O. The direct path at 1317 already uses the Memory/ValueTask overload. #434 reports 'an allocation per underlying buffer fill rather than per caller read' with the allocating frames not yet identified.

**Failure scenario.** 1 MiB body read in 1 KiB pieces: 256 refills, each allocating FillBufferAsync's Task<int> plus the stream's Task<int>; on Mono/Boehm this is steady garbage on the download hot path (the #434 gate measures about 42 KB per MiB).

## Suggested fix
Return ValueTask<int> from FillBufferAsync and read through Stream.ReadAsync(Memory<byte>, CancellationToken); race the ValueTask's awaiter (ConfiguredValueTaskAwaitable<int>.ConfiguredValueTaskAwaiter) instead of the Task awaiter in ReadBodyAsync. Then confirm against the #434 frame-counter gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] FillBufferAsync returns ValueTask<int> and reads through Stream.ReadAsync(Memory<byte>, CancellationToken)
- [ ] The body race awaits the ValueTask awaiter instead of a Task awaiter
- [ ] The #434 frame-counter gate for http11_streaming_body_source_read and the chunked scenario shows the per-read allocation reduction, recorded in the PR
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [HTTP/1.1] Chunk-size lines are parsed leniently: bare LF, EOF, bare CR, leading whitespace and trailing garbage are accepted
body:
## Summary
ReadChunkSizeAsync ends a line at the first LF, parses a partial line at EOF, skips leading SP/HTAB/CR/LF and ignores everything after the first space, so '5<LF>', ' 5' and '5 <NUL>junk' all mean 5. RFC 9112 Section 7.1 requires chunk-size = 1*HEXDIG, optional extensions and CRLF. A client that frames differently from an intermediary can desynchronize a keep-alive connection.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:1535`

## Problem
ReadChunkSizeAsync ends the line at the first LF (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1220-1228) and, at EOF with a partial line, parses what it has (1254-1259). ParseChunkSizeFromBuffer strips an optional CR, cuts at ';', skips leading SP/HTAB/CR/LF (1552-1554), ends the token at the first SP/HTAB and ignores everything after it (1556-1562), and trims CR from the token end (1565-1566). So '5<LF>', ' 5', '5 6', '5<CR>;x' and '5 <NUL>junk' all mean 5. The string variant ParseChunkSizeLine used by ConnectReplyReader behaves the same (761-775). RFC 9112 Section 7.1: chunk = chunk-size [ chunk-ext ] CRLF with chunk-size = 1*HEXDIG; the bare-LF allowance of Section 2.2 is for the start-line and fields.

**Failure scenario.** Client and an intermediary disagree on where a chunk-size line ends (the same parsing gap behind the 2025 bare-LF chunk-extension advisories on the server side): the client keeps a keep-alive connection in a framing state the intermediary does not share. Also, a truncated stream ending in a partial size line is reported from the following read rather than as a truncated size line.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Sections 2.2, 7.1, 7.1.1

## Suggested fix
Require CRLF after the size line, allow only HEXDIG followed by optional BWS + ';' extensions, reject bare CR and trailing garbage, and treat EOF before the terminator as an incomplete message. The fuzz corpus under Tools~/fuzz should get the rejected shapes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Chunk-size lines require CRLF, allow only HEXDIG followed by optional BWS and ';' extensions, and reject bare CR, bare LF and trailing garbage with FormatException
- [ ] EOF before the terminator is reported as an incomplete message
- [ ] ConnectReplyReader's ParseChunkSizeLine follows the same rule
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it plus rejected shapes added to the Tools~/fuzz corpus

title: [HTTP/1.1] Debug.Assert with an interpolated message formats a string on every header append in DEBUG builds
body:
## Summary
EncodingHelper.GetLatin1Bytes builds its Debug.Assert message with string interpolation, which is evaluated on every call when DEBUG is defined, even if the assertion passes. PooledHeaderWriter.Append calls it about 45 times per request, so Editor and Development Builds allocate several KB per request and distort allocation gates. Release players are unaffected.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Internal/EncodingHelper.cs:32`

## Problem
GetLatin1Bytes calls Debug.Assert(destination.Length >= value.Length, $"Destination span is too small: need {value.Length} bytes, got {destination.Length}.") (32-33). The interpolated argument is evaluated before the call whenever DEBUG is defined (two boxed ints and a formatted string), whether or not the assertion fails. PooledHeaderWriter.Append(string) calls it for every request-line part, header name, separator and value (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:546-555).

**Failure scenario.** Editor with debug code optimization or a Development Build: a request with 10 headers runs about 45 Append(string) calls and allocates as many formatted strings (several KB per request), which distorts allocation profiles and Editor allocation gates of the send path; release players are unaffected.

## Suggested fix
Use a constant message, or guard with 'if (destination.Length < value.Length) throw ...' so no string is built on the success path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] GetLatin1Bytes builds no string on the success path (constant message or an explicit length check that throws)
- [ ] Allocation per request in a DEBUG build no longer includes formatted assertion strings, measured in a test
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Transport] RawSocketTransport public constructors leave pool ownership and the TLS backend ambiguous and have no XML docs
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport has three public constructors with no XML docs on two of them. Dispose disposes whatever TcpConnectionPool it was given although the pool is a public, shareable type, and tlsBackend is stored separately from the pool's own backend and used only for proxy CONNECT tunnels. A pool shared by two transports is closed by the first disposal, and a pool and tlsBackend can disagree.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:47`

## Problem
Three public constructors (:42, 47, 55); only the first has a summary and it says 'retained for binary compatibility' although the package version is 1.0.0-pre.1 (package.json:4). The transport disposes whatever pool it was given (Dispose, :2425-2432: _pool?.Dispose()) with no ownsPool flag and no documentation, while TcpConnectionPool is a public type that callers can construct and share (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:269). tlsBackend is stored separately from the pool's own backend (:70-75) and is used only for the TLS handshake inside CONNECT tunnels (:1455) and the Auto viability mark (:1464), so a transport built with a pool configured for one backend and the default tlsBackend handshakes direct connections with the pool's backend and tunnelled ones with Auto. DispatchAsync (:141) and Dispose (:2425) carry no docs; CLAUDE.md section 4 requires XML docs on public API.

**Failure scenario.** A project creates one TcpConnectionPool and passes it to two transports (for example to use different Http2Options per client); disposing the first client closes every connection of the second. Or it configures the pool for one TLS backend and gets a different one for requests that go through a proxy tunnel.

## Suggested fix
Document ownership and add an explicit ownsPool parameter (default true to keep behaviour), take the TLS backend from the pool instead of a second parameter (or reject a mismatch), drop the compatibility overload before 1.0, and add XML docs to the public members.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An explicit ownsPool parameter (default true) controls whether Dispose disposes the pool, and the ownership is documented
- [ ] The TLS backend is taken from the pool or a mismatch is rejected with a clear exception
- [ ] The 'binary compatibility' overload is removed before 1.0 and all public constructors have XML docs
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it for a shared pool surviving the disposal of one transport

title: [Packaging] RawSocketTransport always constructs Http2ConnectionManager, so HTTP/2 ships in builds that cannot negotiate h2
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport creates an Http2ConnectionManager in its constructor and names Http2Connection, Http2ConnectionManager and Http2RetryableRequestException directly in its dispatch paths. On the default SslStream backend ALPN is never negotiated on Unity runtimes, so h2 is unreachable, yet about 8,358 lines of HTTP/2 code are compiled and linked into every player. Titles that only use HTTP/1.1 cannot leave HTTP/2 out and the HTTP/1.1 dispatch code cannot be read or tested without HTTP/2 routing interleaved.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:74`

## Problem
The constructor always creates the manager (:74) and every dispatch path names Http2Connection / Http2ConnectionManager / Http2RetryableRequestException directly (:204-282, 583-646, 865-992, 1133-1149); there is no interface, define or separate asmdef between them (the only #if directives in the non-vendored Transport sources are platform switches). ProbeCapabilities documents that SslStream never negotiates ALPN on Unity's runtimes and that HTTP/2 therefore needs the BouncyCastle provider (:126-134), which is opt-in behind TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE (#258; #429 tracks a native ALPN backend). In the default configuration lease.Connection.NegotiatedAlpnProtocol == 'h2' (:622) is therefore never true, yet Runtime/Transport/Http2 (23 files, 8,358 lines: HPACK encoder/decoder with static and Huffman tables, flow control, stream pool, SingleReaderChannel and Http2ResponseBodySource, the last two additionally preserved in link.xml:65-66) is compiled into TurboHTTP.Transport, statically reachable from the transport, and each transport instance allocates a manager.

**Failure scenario.** A mobile title on the default SslStream backend (no BouncyCastle define) can only ever speak HTTP/1.1 but ships the complete HTTP/2 implementation in the IL2CPP output of every architecture; there is no switch to leave it out, and the HTTP/1.1 dispatch code cannot be read or tested without the HTTP/2 routing interleaved in it.

## Suggested fix
Put HTTP/2 dispatch behind a small internal seam (for example an IAlpnProtocolDispatcher with TryGetExisting / Adopt(lease) / ShouldRetry) held as a nullable field, and register the implementation from the assembly or define that provides an ALPN-capable TLS provider (the BouncyCastle glue today, the native backend of #429 later). Measure with a Stripping High build before and after.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HTTP/2 dispatch in RawSocketTransport goes through a small internal seam held as a nullable field; the default (non-ALPN) configuration does not construct an Http2ConnectionManager.
- [ ] The implementation is registered only by the assembly or define that provides an ALPN-capable TLS provider, and a build without it contains no reachable reference to the HTTP/2 stack from the HTTP/1.1 path.
- [ ] Behaviour with the BouncyCastle provider is unchanged: h2 is still negotiated and dispatched.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ shows that a transport built without the HTTP/2 dispatcher serves HTTP/1.1 requests and does not allocate an HTTP/2 manager.
- [ ] Build-size effect on an IL2CPP player is measured and recorded in the PR.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: Facts hold: the constructor always creates Http2ConnectionManager (RawSocketTransport.cs:74), dispatch names Http2 types directly (:204-282, :583-646, proxy path :865-992), there is no interface, define or asmdef seam (the only #if in non-vendored Transport sources are platform switches and the NET5 attribute guard), and Runtime/Transport/Http2 is 23 files / 8,358 lines. The comment at :126-128 states SslStream never negotiates ALPN on Unity's runtimes, so without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE the 'h2' branch is not taken in a player. The manager constructor is three field assignments (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:45-50), so the per-instance cost is nil; the whole impact is IL2CPP code size, which nobody has measured, hence plausible. Severity lowered: not a defect, and the premise is time-limited because #429 (native ALPN backend, v1.2) is meant to make HTTP/2 reachable by default and #258/#428 cover the BouncyCastle opt-in; a seam is only worth it if a Stripping High size diff shows a material saving. Not tracked as a build-size item by any open issue.

Related: #258, #429, [[R11-http1-design-06]].

title: [HTTP/1.1] Expect: 100-continue path treats a sent zero-byte chunked body as unsent, so a POST can be replayed
body:
## Summary
On the Expect: 100-continue split path the transport never marks the message as written and relies on HasCommittedBodyBytes, which is only set for bodies with at least one data byte. A chunked request whose body yields no data still writes the terminating 0-chunk, but the retry predicates consider nothing sent. A non-idempotent request such as POST can therefore be replayed on a new connection after the server already received a complete message.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:284`

## Problem
The split path never calls MarkMessageWritten (documented at Http11RequestSerializer.cs:25-31) and relies on HasCommittedBodyBytes, which is only set by RecordBodyBytesWritten for bytesWritten > 0 (44-51). WriteChunkedBodyAsync for a body that yields no data writes only '0 CRLF [trailers] CRLF' (419-441) and records nothing. ExpectContinueHelper.HasRequestBody is true for unknown-length and trailer-only bodies (ExpectContinueHelper.cs:15-27), so they take this path. Afterwards CanRetryHttp11RequestAfterTransportFailure (RawSocketTransport.cs:284-300) and ShouldRetryWithoutExpectation (1657-1669) both see 'no body byte committed'.

**Failure scenario.** POST with Expect: 100-continue and an unknown-length replayable body that turns out empty (or an empty body with request trailers) on a reused connection: the server sends 100, receives the complete request, processes it, and the connection dies before the response (or the server answers 417 after the body). The transport replays the POST on a fresh connection, or repeats it without Expect, and the side effect happens twice.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 9.2.2

## Suggested fix
Have TrySendRequestBodyAsync mark the write state as 'message written' once SerializeBodyAsync and the flush completed, and make both retry predicates check HasWrittenCompleteMessage on the Expect path too.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After SerializeBodyAsync and the flush complete on the Expect path, the write state is marked as a completely written message.
- [ ] Both retry predicates check HasWrittenCompleteMessage on the Expect path, so a non-idempotent request with an empty chunked body is not replayed after a stale-connection failure once the terminator was sent.
- [ ] Idempotent requests keep their existing retry behaviour.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ using a loopback server that closes after receiving the empty chunked body fails before the fix (second request observed) and passes after.

title: [HTTP/1.1] IOException from the caller's request body is retried as a stale-connection failure and reported as NetworkError
body:
## Summary
IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure accepts any IOException thrown out of DispatchOnLeaseAsync. That includes the serializer's own 'Request body ended before the declared Content-Length was fully produced' error and IOExceptions raised by the application's body source. Such faults are retried as if the reused socket had died and are finally reported as NetworkError, hiding a caller bug behind a retryable network failure.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:356`

## Problem
IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure accepts any IOException (RawSocketTransport.cs:356-363) thrown out of DispatchOnLeaseAsync, including the serializer's own 'Request body ended before the declared Content-Length was fully produced.' (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:389-393) and IOExceptions from the body session's ReadAsync (384-387, 421-424). On a reused connection with an idempotent or not-yet-committed request the catch at 665-669 opens a fresh connection and sends again; otherwise MapDispatchAttemptFailure maps the IOException to UHttpErrorType.NetworkError (805-806). The connection itself is correctly destroyed in both cases.

**Failure scenario.** PUT with a file/stream body whose declared length is larger than what the stream produces (or whose read fails with a disk IOException) on a reused connection: head plus partial body are sent twice to the server on two connections, and the caller receives NetworkError, which a retry interceptor treats as retryable, for what is a local body error.

## Suggested fix
Wrap body-source failures in the serializer (a dedicated internal exception type carrying the inner error) so the transport can tell them from socket I/O, exclude them from the stale retry and report them as InvalidRequest/Unknown rather than NetworkError.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Failures raised while producing the request body are wrapped in a dedicated internal exception type that carries the inner error and are excluded from IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure.
- [ ] They surface as UHttpException with InvalidRequest or Unknown, not NetworkError, and the body source is not invoked a second time.
- [ ] Genuine socket IOExceptions on a reused connection are still retried as before.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a body source that throws IOException and a short-declared Content-Length body fails before the fix and passes after.

title: [Transport] RawSocketTransport leaves its Expect-injected request copy in context.Request instead of restoring the original
body:
## Summary
PrepareEffectiveRequest clones the request, adds Expect: 100-continue and calls context.UpdateRequest with the clone; the 417 repeat does it again. The caller's original request is never restored, unlike the documented request-mutation contract, so later pipeline stages and the caller observe a wire-level header the user did not set.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:410`

## Problem
PrepareEffectiveRequest clones the request (a header clone plus a new metadata dictionary, Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:514-526), adds Expect: 100-continue and calls context.UpdateRequest(effectiveRequest) (:410-412); the 417 repeat does the same again (:538-539). Neither path restores the caller's request in a finally block. architecture.md ('Request mutation') requires code that rewrites a request to call UpdateRequest and restore the original in finally; every interceptor does (for example Runtime/Middleware/DefaultHeadersInterceptor.cs:47 and 65, Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:75 and 87). The transport also overwrites context.Request in the non-inject case (:404-405).

**Failure scenario.** With no rewriting interceptor in the chain (the default client), after a large upload context.Request is the transport's private copy: handlers and observers that read it at OnResponseStart or when the body is disposed see an Expect header the application never set (and, after a 417 repeat, a third instance without it), on a request instance different from the one the caller holds.

## Suggested fix
Do not publish the transport's wire-level copy through the context: pass the injected expectation as a serializer input (a flag on the dispatch), or restore the original request in a finally in DispatchAsync.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After DispatchAsync completes (success, error or cancellation) context.Request is the request the caller supplied, without the injected Expect header.
- [ ] The injected expectation is passed to the serializer as dispatch input or restored in a finally block, and the 417 repeat follows the same rule.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ asserts that context.Request has no Expect header after a request that triggered injection, and fails before the fix.

title: [Transport] MapDispatchAttemptFailure unwraps HandlerCallbackException and the handler gets OnResponseError twice
body:
## Summary
HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper.ReportFailure wraps an exception thrown by the handler's own OnResponseError in HandlerCallbackException. MapDispatchAttemptFailure returns its InnerException, and when that is a UHttpException DispatchAsync reports it to the same handler again. A handler that already failed in OnResponseError receives a second OnResponseError call for the same failure.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:791`

## Problem
HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper.ReportFailure wraps an exception thrown by the handler's own OnResponseError in HandlerCallbackException (Runtime/Core/Pipeline/HandlerCallbackSafetyWrapper.cs:119-126). MapDispatchAttemptFailure returns handlerFault.InnerException (:791-793), which DispatchAttemptAsync rethrows (:752-754). DispatchAsync then runs catch (UHttpException ex) { context.RecordEvent('RequestFailed'); handler.OnResponseError(ex, context); } (:178-182) on the raw, unwrapped handler. architecture.md states that handler faults are 'never re-reported to the same handler'. The existing test (Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1/RawSocketTransportTests.cs:302) covers only an InvalidOperationException thrown from OnResponseError.

**Failure scenario.** A handler whose OnResponseError rethrows the UHttpException it was given (a simple way to surface the error through the dispatch task) is called once by the safety wrapper and a second time by DispatchAsync, and the timeline records 'RequestFailed' twice (:792 and :180).

## Suggested fix
Keep the HandlerCallbackException type until DispatchAsync and rethrow its inner exception there without calling the handler, or have MapDispatchAttemptFailure return a wrapper that is not a UHttpException.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A HandlerCallbackException keeps its type until DispatchAsync, which rethrows the inner exception without calling the handler again.
- [ ] OnResponseError is invoked at most once per request, including when the handler's own callback throws a UHttpException.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a handler whose OnResponseError throws UHttpException counts callbacks and fails before the fix (count 2).

title: [HTTP/1.1] Failures use BCL exception types classified by three mappers, so caller errors become retryable NetworkError
body:
## Summary
The HTTP/1.1 layer throws FormatException, IOException, NotSupportedException and InvalidOperationException, and three sites (MapDispatchAttemptFailure, the body source and the CONNECT reader) translate them independently, one by matching message text. The mapping is inconsistent: request-shape faults caused by the caller can become retryable NetworkError, and malformed responses can become Unknown depending on the path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:805`

## Problem
The HTTP/1.1 layer throws FormatException / IOException / NotSupportedException / InvalidOperationException (e.g. Http11ResponseParser.cs:274, 286, 518; Http11RequestSerializer.cs:249, 391) and three sites translate them independently: MapDispatchAttemptFailure (RawSocketTransport.cs:794-828), the five-clause ladder in Http11ResponseBodySource.ReadAsync (:155-226; the IOException and SocketException clauses are identical, and the 'Malformed HTTP response:' / 'Unsupported HTTP response:' / 'Request timed out after' strings repeat RawSocketTransport.cs:813, 818, 835) and ConnectReplyReader (:208-214, 310-313). Stale-connection detection is IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure = ex is IOException || SocketException || a FormatException whose Message equals 'Empty HTTP status line' (:356-387; the parser comment at Http11ResponseParser.cs:269-271 and Http11ResponseParserStrictnessTests.cs:70 pin the text). Because the single catch in DispatchAttemptAsync (:746) covers request serialization and response parsing alike, the type cannot tell who failed: (a) the serializer's own IOException 'Request body ended before the declared Content-Length was fully produced' (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:391) passes IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure and is then mapped to NetworkError (:805-806), which UHttpError.IsRetryable treats as retryable (Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:72-74); (b) ValidateTrailerCompatibility's InvalidOperationException (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:249; WithRequestTrailers on a known-length body, which HTTP/2 accepts) falls to the default arm and becomes UHttpErrorType.Unknown (:827-828) while the sibling caller error HttpFieldValidationException gets InvalidRequest (:822-826); (c) a FormatException or NotSupportedException thrown by a caller's body stream or factory is reported as 'Malformed/Unsupported HTTP response' (:809-818); (d) an ObjectDisposedException from a disposed transport (:435-436) escapes DispatchAsync as a raw exception because its catch only handles UHttpException and OperationCanceledException (:178-187). No test covers (a); Http11SerializerTests.cs:296-320 assert the raw InvalidOperationException at serializer level only.

**Failure scenario.** PUT with WithBodyFactory(factory, contentLength: 100) whose stream yields 50 bytes, on a reused connection: attempt 1 writes the head and 50 bytes, throws IOException, is classified as a stale connection (TransportRetryStale), the connection is destroyed, a new one is dialled and the partial upload is sent again; the caller then gets NetworkError, which a Retry interceptor replays again. A caller bug is reported as a network failure and multiplied into several partial uploads. Separately, request.WithBody(bytes).WithRequestTrailers(...) fails with Unknown on HTTP/1.1 only.

## Suggested fix
Give the HTTP/1.1 layer its own internal failure type with a kind (ClosedBeforeStatusLine, MalformedResponse, UnsupportedFraming) and a separate type for request-body/request-shape faults, and map them in one shared function used by the dispatch path, the body source and the CONNECT reader. Classify body-source and request-shape failures as non-retryable InvalidRequest and never as stale.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The HTTP/1.1 layer uses an internal failure type with a kind (ClosedBeforeStatusLine, MalformedResponse, UnsupportedFraming) and a separate type for request-body or request-shape faults.
- [ ] One shared mapping function is used by the dispatch path, the body source and the CONNECT reader, with no matching on message strings.
- [ ] Caller faults map to InvalidRequest and are not retried; malformed or truncated responses map to the documented UHttpError values.
- [ ] Deterministic NUnit tests under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ cover each kind on all three paths and fail before the change where the mapping differs.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: best-practices.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Sub-claims (a)-(c) traced, (d) rejected. (a) The serializer's own IOException for a short body (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:389-393) passes IsStaleReusedConnectionFailure (RawSocketTransport.cs:356-363, type test only) and, for an idempotent replayable request on a reused lease, triggers the stale retry (665-714) and a second partial upload, then maps to NetworkError (805-806), which UHttpError.IsRetryable treats as retryable (Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:69-74). No test covers it (the message appears only in the serializer and Http2Connection.Send.cs:283). (b) ValidateTrailerCompatibility throws InvalidOperationException (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:249); neither WithRequestTrailers (UHttpRequest.cs:292-307) nor SetRequestTrailers (UHttpRequestBody.cs:47-63) checks the body length, and the default arm maps it to Unknown (827-828) while HttpFieldValidationException gets InvalidRequest (822-826). (c) The single catch at 746 covers serialization and parsing, so a FormatException/NotSupportedException from a caller body stream is reported as a malformed/unsupported response (809-818). Stale detection does rest on the message string 'Empty HTTP status line' (380-387). (d) ObjectDisposedException from a disposed transport (435-436) escaping is the normal .NET contract, not a defect.

title: [Proxy] A failed CONNECT drops the proxy status and headers: 407 is InvalidRequest, other statuses retryable NetworkError
body:
## Summary
EstablishConnectTunnelAsync throws UHttpException(InvalidRequest) for 407 and UHttpException(NetworkError, 'CONNECT tunnel failed with status N.') for all other failures, with the code only in the message text. UHttpError.StatusCode exists but is not set and the proxy's reply headers are dropped. Callers and retry policy cannot tell a permanent 403 from a transient 503.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1507`

## Problem
EstablishConnectTunnelAsync throws UHttpException(InvalidRequest, 'Proxy authentication required (407); ...') (:1507-1509) and UHttpException(NetworkError, 'CONNECT tunnel failed with status N.') (:1512-1514). UHttpError has a StatusCode property (Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:50-60) that is not set here, and the reply headers (Proxy-Authenticate, Retry-After) are dropped. For an http:// target through the same proxy a 407 or 403 is delivered to the handler as a normal response with its body (DispatchViaProxyAsync, :879-927), as the error model in CLAUDE.md section 3 requires for HTTP 4xx/5xx. NetworkError is retryable (UHttpError.cs:72-74).

**Failure scenario.** A proxy answers CONNECT with 403 (destination blocked by policy): the application receives a NetworkError, a Retry interceptor replays the request against the proxy up to its limit, and code cannot distinguish 403 from 502/503 or read Proxy-Authenticate to tell the user which scheme the proxy wants except by parsing the English message.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Sections 9.3.6 and 15.5.8

## Suggested fix
Carry the status code (UHttpError.StatusCode) and the reply headers on the exception and map by class: 407 without usable credentials and other 4xx as non-retryable, 5xx as retryable. Document that CONNECT failures are errors rather than responses.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The CONNECT failure exception carries the proxy status code (StatusCode) and the reply headers (for example Proxy-Authenticate, Retry-After).
- [ ] 407 without usable credentials and other 4xx are non-retryable; 5xx is retryable; the classification is documented, including that CONNECT failures are errors rather than responses.
- [ ] Proxy reply headers are redacted where logged or attached to exceptions per the redaction policy.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a loopback proxy answering 403, 407 and 503 asserts the status code and error class and fails before the fix.

## Context

title: [Transport] Streaming body reads have no idle bound, so a half-open connection pins its lease and host permit
body:
## Summary
For streaming responses the body source gets CancellationToken.None as its transport token and the request timeout CTS is disposed once headers are returned. A read without a consumer token is therefore unbounded: if the peer goes silent without closing, the connection lease and the per-host permit stay held until the consumer's own token fires, which may never happen.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1826`

## Problem
For a streaming response the body source gets CancellationToken.None as its transport token (1826-1830; Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:26-28), and the request timeout CTS is disposed when DispatchCoreAsync returns at the headers (439). A read with no consumer token therefore goes through the non-raced path (Http11ResponseParser.cs:1316-1317, 1415-1417) and nothing but the peer or the consumer can end it. The lease (and the per-host semaphore permit it owns) is released only by CompleteBody/CloseBody (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:660-684).

**Failure scenario.** Mobile client downloads with 'await stream.CopyToAsync(file)' (no token); the device changes network or a NAT drops the mapping without FIN/RST (platform.md: half-open connections after Wi-Fi <-> LTE). The read never completes; the connection and its per-host permit stay held, and after MaxConnectionsPerHost such downloads every further request to that host queues forever.

## Suggested fix
Give streaming body reads an optional idle timeout in StreamingOptions (applied per read by the reader race, off or generous by default) and document that a token-less streaming read is otherwise unbounded.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] StreamingOptions has an optional idle timeout applied per body read by the reader race; the default is off or generous and is documented.
- [ ] On idle expiry the read fails with UHttpException(Timeout), the connection is disposed and the lease and permit are released exactly once.
- [ ] Documentation states that a token-less streaming read is otherwise unbounded.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a loopback server that stops sending mid-body asserts the timeout and lease release, and fails before the fix (read never completes).

## Context
