title: [HTTP/1.1] Connection is pooled after a request with Connection: close when the response does not echo close
body:
## Summary
The serializer forwards a caller's Connection header verbatim, but connection reuse is decided only from the response. If the server answers a request that carried Connection: close without repeating close, the connection goes back to the pool even though RFC 9112 section 9.6 says the sender of close must close the connection after the response. The next request may then fail on a socket the peer is closing.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1832`

## Problem
The serializer forwards a caller Connection header verbatim (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:320-337; keep-alive is only auto-added when none is set, 359-360). Reuse is decided only from the response: Http11ResponseParser.IsKeepAlive (Http11ResponseParser.cs:598-644) -> ParsedResponseHead.KeepAlive -> Http11ResponseBodySource._keepAlive (Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:61) -> CompleteBody calls _lease.ReturnToPool() (667-671). DispatchOnLeaseAsync (RawSocketTransport.cs:1798-1840) never looks at the request's Connection field; rg for 'close' in Runtime/Transport finds only the response parser and ConnectReplyReader.

**Failure scenario.** Caller sets 'Connection: close' (to force a fresh connection per call, or behind a load balancer that needs it). Server answers 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 2' without a Connection field and then closes, as the RFC tells it to. The client pools the connection; the next request is written into a socket the server is closing. A non-idempotent POST whose bytes were committed cannot be retried (CanRetryHttp11RequestAfterTransportFailure, 284-300) and fails with NetworkError. If the server does not close, the client keeps using a connection it promised to close.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.6

## Suggested fix
In DispatchOnLeaseAsync, force head.KeepAlive = false when the sent request's Connection field contains the 'close' token (reuse ExpectContinueHelper.HeaderValueContainsToken). Add a loopback test asserting AcceptCount == 2 for two sequential requests when the first carries Connection: close.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] In DispatchOnLeaseAsync, ParsedResponseHead.KeepAlive is forced to false when the sent request's Connection field contains the 'close' token (using ExpectContinueHelper.HeaderValueContainsToken).
- [ ] The connection is closed and not pooled after such a request, regardless of the response headers.
- [ ] Requests without Connection: close keep their current reuse behaviour.
- [ ] A loopback NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ asserts AcceptCount == 2 for two sequential requests when the first carries Connection: close, failing before the fix.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-protocol-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. A caller 'Connection: close' is forwarded verbatim (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:320-337, pinned by Http11SerializerTests.cs:164-167); keep-alive is decided only from the response (Http11ResponseParser.IsKeepAlive 598-644 -> head.KeepAlive -> Http11ResponseBodySource._keepAlive :61 -> CompleteBody ReturnToPool :667-671). DispatchOnLeaseAsync (RawSocketTransport.cs:1765-1844) never inspects the request's Connection field; rg for the close token in Runtime/Transport finds only the response parser (:620) and ConnectReplyReader (:44). RFC 9112 Section 9.6: a client that sends close MUST NOT send further requests on that connection. Mitigation that keeps it at medium: most servers echo close, and the pool's IsAlive/HasUnexpectedData check (TcpConnectionPool.cs:510-519) catches a FIN that already arrived; the failure needs a server that does not echo and a next request issued before the FIN is seen.

title: [Transport] Unreferenced members and an unreachable branch ship in RawSocketTransport and tests target the dead copies
body:
## Summary
The transport contains members with no callers in Runtime, Tests or Tools (DispatchOnStreamAsync, SendOnStreamAsync, EmitParsedResponseAsync, MapException, PooledHeaderWriter.AppendInt, EnumerateBodySegments, AbandonableTask.Observe), a buffered response path and a chunked CONNECT drain that cannot be reached. Chunk-framing tests, the h1-response fuzz target and soak counters exercise these dead copies instead of the code that runs in production.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1846`

## Problem
No caller in Runtime/, Tests/ or Tools~ (rg): RawSocketTransport.DispatchOnStreamAsync (:1846), SendOnStreamAsync (:2366), EmitParsedResponseAsync (:1587, whose XML summary at :1583-1586 describes a different method), MapException (:190-192), Http11RequestSerializer.PooledHeaderWriter.AppendInt (Http11RequestSerializer.cs:576-598), ParsedResponse.EnumerateBodySegments (Http11ResponseParser.cs:85-99). Test-only: Http11ResponseParser.ParseAsync and the buffered body readers behind it (the runtime lens reports that path), AbandonableTask.Observe (Runtime/Transport/Internal/AbandonableTask.cs:24-28; the class is a pure forwarder to Core's AbandonOnCancel) and ConnectReply.IsChunked (ConnectReplyReader.cs:38). Unreachable in production: the Transfer-Encoding branch of ConnectReplyReader.DrainBodyCoreAsync and DrainChunkedAsync (:163-178, 195-238), because both callers drain only after CanRetryOnSameConnection, which requires Headers.Get('Transfer-Encoding') == null (:57-61; RawSocketTransport.cs:1482-1486; Runtime/WebSocket.Transport/ProxyTunnelConnector.cs:120-128); with it Http11ResponseParser.ParseChunkSizeLine and the char overload of ParseChunkSizeToken (:761-775, 795-814) have no production caller. Side effects: the chunk-framing tests (Http11ResponseParserTests.cs:283-292, 648-760) and the 'h1-response' fuzz target (Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:72-95) exercise the buffered decoder production never runs; the soak leak assertion on ParsedResponsePool (Tests/Runtime/Performance/SoakShortTests.cs:38, 65; Tools~/soak/SoakClient.cs:296) cannot fail because nothing rents from that pool; architecture.md still lists 'Snapshot status/headers before returning a pooled ParsedResponse' as a live contract.

**Failure scenario.** A change to chunk-size or trailer handling is verified green against ReadChunkedBodyAsync / DrainChunkedAsync while the shipped decoder (Http11ResponseBodySource.ReadChunkedAsync) is a different implementation; reviewers and the soak gate take assurance from code that never runs. About 570 lines stay in the assembly (http1-design-07 explains why the linker does not remove them).

## Suggested fix
Delete the unreferenced members and the buffered path, re-point the chunk-framing tests and the h1-response fuzz target at ParseHeadAsync plus Http11ResponseBodySource, remove the ParsedResponsePool soak counters, and either delete the chunked CONNECT drain or let CanRetryOnSameConnection accept chunked 407 bodies so the branch is used.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The unreferenced members and the buffered path are deleted; the chunked CONNECT drain is either deleted or made reachable with a test.
- [ ] Chunk-framing tests and the h1-response fuzz target are re-pointed at ParseHeadAsync plus Http11ResponseBodySource, and the ParsedResponsePool soak counters are removed.
- [ ] check.sh passes with no new analyzer warnings and the public API is unchanged.
- [ ] The re-pointed tests under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ still cover the chunk framing cases they covered before.

title: [HTTP/1.1] First-byte watchdog allocates two CancellationTokenSources and a timer per request on a reused connection
body:
## Summary
ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout defaults to 10 s, so AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync arms the watchdog for every idempotent replayable request on a reused connection, which is the ordinary keep-alive GET. Each call creates two CancellationTokenSources, a timer and several registrations, adding avoidable allocations to the most common request path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1987`

## Problem
ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout defaults to 10 s (Runtime/Core/PlatformConfig.cs:42-44), so GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout (344-354) arms the watchdog for every idempotent replayable request on a reused connection, i.e. the normal keep-alive GET. AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync then creates 'new CancellationTokenSource(firstByteTimeout)' (CTS + Timer), a linked CTS over ct and the watchdog (two registrations), and a RegisterDisposeOnCancel registration (1987-1992); the read itself goes through EnsureBufferedAsync -> FillBufferAsync -> AbandonableTask.WaitAsync, which adds a TaskCompletionSource, another registration and a Task.WhenAny (Runtime/Core/Internal/AbandonOnCancel.cs:67-70). This is on top of the per-request linked timeout CTS and timer (439-440) and the dispose-on-cancel registration (1776).

**Failure scenario.** A client polling an API over keep-alive: each request creates 3 CTS objects, 2 timers and about 5 token registrations before the first response byte, roughly 1 KB of short-lived objects plus timer-queue churn per request on the default path.

## Suggested fix
Use one CTS: CreateLinkedTokenSource(ct) with CancelAfter(firstByteTimeout), tell the watchdog from the caller by ct.IsCancellationRequested, and register the dispose-on-cancel on that one token; or reuse the request's timeout CTS with a second deadline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The watchdog uses one linked CancellationTokenSource with CancelAfter(firstByteTimeout), distinguishing watchdog expiry from caller cancellation by ct.IsCancellationRequested, or reuses the request's timeout CTS with a second deadline.
- [ ] Allocations per keep-alive GET on a reused connection drop by at least one CancellationTokenSource and one timer, measured and recorded in the PR.
- [ ] Stale-connection detection and the timeout error semantics are unchanged.
- [ ] Existing ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout tests under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ pass, with a deterministic test asserting caller cancellation is not reported as a watchdog timeout.

title: [Architecture] RawSocketTransport owns the HTTP/1.1 exchange state machines and the body decoder is welded to ConnectionLease
body:
## Summary
The Expect: 100-continue state machine, one-shot send, 1xx handling and stale-retry logic are private to RawSocketTransport instead of living under Http1/, and Http11ResponseBodySource is tied to ConnectionLease. They cannot be exercised without a pool and sockets, which makes them hard to test and review.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:2018`

## Problem
HTTP/1.1-specific logic that is private to RawSocketTransport instead of living in Http1/: the Expect: 100-continue state machine (SendOnLeaseWithExpectContinueAsync, WaitForAbortedReadAsync, ReadExpectContinueFinalHeadAsync, CompleteExpectContinueHead, TrySendRequestBodyAsync and helpers, :2018-2364, about 350 lines), the 417 repeat (:1640-1669, 531-541), the stale-connection policy and first-byte watchdog (:284-300, 344-395, 1981-2016), the forward-proxy Basic-407 interception and drain (:1671-1763, 1809-1824) and CONNECT (:1429-1568), next to registration, cleartext policy, HTTP/2 routing/replay and error mapping. Nothing in Http1/ composes 'send the request, maybe wait for 100, read the head'; the only stream-level seam, DispatchOnStreamAsync(Stream ...) (:1846), is unreferenced. Visible consequences: the direct and proxy retry blocks are copies that diverged (http1-design-01); HTTP/2 re-implements the Expect wait and lacks the 417 repeat (open #391); Http11ResponseBodySource fuses the chunked / length / close decoders with lease return, drain policy and timeout mapping, so the fuzz target and the unit tests must create a real Socket, a PooledConnection and a ConnectionLease with a null pool and a SemaphoreSlim(0,1) to decode bytes from a MemoryStream (Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:110-124; Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySourceTests.cs:37-40, 246-249); and a BufferedStreamReader is created per response (:1941, 1949, 2026) although its read-ahead belongs to the connection, which is the root of the 'bytes after a complete response are discarded and the connection pooled' defect the protocol and runtime lenses report. Open #182 lists four oversized files, the largest 929 lines; this file and Http11ResponseParser.cs (1,610 lines) are not on it.

**Failure scenario.** Every Expect / 417 / stale-retry behaviour needs a loopback TcpListener test (RawSocketTransportTests.cs is 2,918 lines), so interleavings such as 'the 100 arrives while the body send fails' are reachable only through timing; a fix in one copy of the retry block does not reach the other (this has already happened); the streaming decoder cannot be reused or unit-tested without pool types.

## Suggested fix
Extract an Http11Exchange in Http1/ that takes (Stream, reader, request, options) and returns a ParsedResponseHead (one-shot send, Expect: 100-continue, 1xx handling), a stale-retry policy object, and split Http11ResponseBodySource into a pure decoder over the reader plus a small owner that settles the lease through a callback; make the reader a per-connection object. Do pure moves first and add both files to #182.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An Http11Exchange in Http1/ takes (Stream, reader, request, options) and returns a ParsedResponseHead, covering one-shot send, Expect: 100-continue and 1xx handling.
- [ ] The stale-retry policy is a separate object and Http11ResponseBodySource is split into a pure decoder over the reader plus a small owner that settles the lease.
- [ ] RawSocketTransport shrinks accordingly; behaviour and the public API are unchanged.
- [ ] New deterministic NUnit tests under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ drive Http11Exchange over in-memory streams without a pool or sockets.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `http1-design-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/http1.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Structural claims check out. RawSocketTransport.cs is 2,434 lines and privately owns the Expect: 100-continue machine (SendOnLeaseWithExpectContinueAsync :2018 through TrySendRequestBodyAsync :2338), the 417 repeat (:1642-1669), stale-connection policy and first-byte watchdog (:284-395, :1981), forward-proxy 407 drain (:1695-1763) and CONNECT (:1429-1568) next to registration, HTTP/2 routing and error mapping. DispatchOnStreamAsync (:1846), SendOnStreamAsync (:2366) and EmitParsedResponseAsync (:1587) have no caller in Runtime, Tests or Tools~ (rg), so Http11ResponseParser.ParseAsync is reached at runtime only from dead code (tests and the fuzz target call it directly). Http11ResponseBodySource does need a real Socket + PooledConnection + ConnectionLease(null, SemaphoreSlim(0,1)) to decode a MemoryStream (Tools~/fuzz/Targets.cs:109-124; Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySourceTests.cs:37-40). A BufferedStreamReader is created per response (:1949, :2026, and inside ParseHeadAsync at Http11ResponseParser.cs:217). RawSocketTransportTests.cs is 2,918 lines. #182 lists four other files (PluginContext, MainThreadDispatcher, UHttpClient, DecompressionHandler), so this is not tracked; #391 confirms the HTTP/2 417 gap cited as a consequence. This is a maintainability/testability finding with no direct runtime failure of its own; I did not re-trace the sibling claims it leans on (http1-design-01 diverged retry copies, discarded read-ahead bytes).

title: [HTTP/1.1] After a local body-send failure on Expect: 100-continue the request waits for a final response until request timeout
body:
## Summary
TrySendRequestBodyAsync captures any body-send exception and returns it. Both continuation branches then wait for a response head bounded only by the request token. When the send failed locally and no response byte is buffered, the request holds its connection and per-host permit for the full request timeout before the send failure is reported.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:2085`

## Problem
TrySendRequestBodyAsync captures any body-send exception and returns it (2338-2364). Both branches then await a response head with only the request token: after a 100, ReadExpectContinueFinalHeadAsync -> ParseHeadAsync(reader, ..., ct) (2085-2092, 2199-2207); after the continue timeout, 'await initialHeadTask' (2114-2122). The captured exception is rethrown only once that read fails ('catch ... when (bodySendException != null)'). The non-Expect path (SerializeAsync, 1925-1931) fails at once on the same error. The #109 test covers a server that answers 413; no test covers a server that stays silent.

**Failure scenario.** Upload with Expect: 100-continue whose source stream throws after part of the declared Content-Length was sent (file read error, producer fault). The server has received an incomplete body and waits for the rest; the client waits for a head. The caller sees the body stream's exception only when request.Timeout fires (30/45 s by default, often minutes for uploads), and the connection, the per-host permit and the reader buffer stay held for that whole time.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 10.1.1

## Suggested fix
When the body send failed before completion and no response byte is buffered, bound the wait for the final head with a short grace period (for example ExpectContinueTimeoutMs), then dispose the connection and surface the send failure.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the body send failed before completion and no response byte is buffered, the wait for the final head is bounded by a short grace period (for example ExpectContinueTimeoutMs).
- [ ] On expiry the connection is disposed and the original send failure is surfaced, with the lease and permit released once.
- [ ] Behaviour when a final response does arrive promptly is unchanged.
- [ ] A deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ with a failing body source and a silent server asserts the failure arrives within the grace period and fails before the fix.

## Context
